       漲價效益持續發酵，4Q26 毛利率續升 : 公司今年 5～6 月起陸續與客戶進行漲
       價協商，並依客戶、產品及訂單狀況逐步反映，且主要針對新接訂單，因此漲
       價效益並非立即反映於營收及毛利率。隨 9～10 月開始陸續 出 貨 漲價後 訂 單 ，
       產品組合持續優化，漲價效益可望逐步挹注毛利率；我們認為由於 9 月營收已
       大致反映前一波漲價，加上新增產能尚未完全開出，預期 10～11 月營收維持
       相 對 穩 定 ， 惟 產 品 組 合 持 續 優 化 ， 漲 價 效 益 仍 可 帶 動 毛 利 率 進 一 步 提 升 。 12
       月營收則仍將受到年度盤點及聖誕假期等季節性因素影響而略有波動，但在高
       毛利產品占比提升及漲價效益持續發酵下，獲利率可望維持高檔，因此我們上
       調 4Q26 營收至 11.1 億元，毛利率至 41.89%，EPS 為 2.1 元。

       2027 年不只量增，更有望迎來價增 :我們認為光頡的高階精密電阻供需緊張格
       局至少延續至 2027 年，除目前部分產品交期仍較過去延長數週、訂單能見度
       已達 2027 年下半年外，高規格產品具較高製程及良率門檻，新供應商短期亦
       難以補足供給。從海外同業 Vishay 近期動態亦可觀察到類似趨勢，公司 2026
       年持續推動價格調整，且部分漲價已逐步反映於財務表現，反映高階電阻供應
       緊張並非單一供應商現象，而是產業供需結構正在改變。

       在需求持續高於供給的環境下，我們認為 2027 年漲價仍具延續空間，且價格
       將逐漸成為客戶取得產能的重要條件，後續調價未必採全面性調整，而可能與
       採購量及產能配置連動。另一方面，光頡新增產能並非單純追求出貨量，而將
       優先配置至高規格、高毛利及價格接受度較高的產品，意味著公司可望同時受
       惠於 ASP 提升及產品組合優化。我們因此認為， 2027 年光頡的獲利成長除了
       來自 AI 需求與產能擴充，漲價及高階產品占比提升將是毛利率與 EPS 進一步
       上修的重要驅動力。

       評價收斂不改獲利上修趨勢，維持買進 : 我們重申光頡買進評等，並上調
       2026/2027 年 EPS 預估至 5.57 元/11.13 元，反映 AI 伺服器放量帶動高階精密
       電阻需求，及交期拉長推升漲價效益，帶動產品組合與獲利能力改善。考量漲
       價效益已逐步反映，後續獲利成長將轉由 AI 需求及產品升級驅動，我們將評
       價基準由原先 2H26～1H27 EPS 調整至 2027 年 EPS，並參考 Vishay 目前約 20
       ～25 倍本益比，將合理本益比由 30 倍下修至 20 倍。

       公司簡介

       光頡成立於 1997 年 10 月，為台灣首家同時具備薄膜/厚膜製程技術及高頻被
       動元件、模組設計開發能力的專業廠商。公司長期深耕薄膜製程技術研發與高
       頻元件整合設計，專注提供符合電子產品高頻化、小型化趨勢需求的整合型被
       動元件及高頻模組等關鍵零組件。生產基地布局涵蓋台灣與中國大陸，其中台
       灣廠區包括新竹科學園區、新竹工業區及高雄二廠、三廠，中國大陸則設有無
       錫及南通生產基地。公司主要競爭者為 Vishay、KOA、國巨(2327)、華新科(2492)
       等 。 2016 年 中國被 動元件 龍頭廣 東風 華高新 科技 策略性 入股 光頡， 目前 持 股
       約 40%，為公司最大股東，有助於強化其在中國市場的布局及產業資源整合能
       力。

       漲價效益持續發酵，4Q26 毛利率續升 : 公司今年 5～6 月起陸續與客戶進行漲
       價協商，並依客戶、產品及訂單狀況逐步反映，且主要針對新接訂單，因此漲
       價效益並非立即反映於營收及毛利率。隨 9～10 月開始陸續 出 貨 漲價後 訂 單 ，
       產品組合持續優化，漲價效益可望逐步挹注毛利率；我們認為由於 9 月營收已
       大致反映前一波漲價，加上新增產能尚未完全開出，預期 10～11 月營收維持
       相 對 穩 定 ， 惟 產 品 組 合 持 續 優 化 ， 漲 價 效 益 仍 可 帶 動 毛 利 率 進 一 步 提 升 。 12
       月營收則仍將受到年度盤點及聖誕假期等季節性因素影響而略有波動，但在高
       毛利產品占比提升及漲價效益持續發酵下，獲利率可望維持高檔，因此我們上
       調 4Q26 營收至 11.1 億元，毛利率至 41.89%，EPS 為 2.1 元。

       2027 年不只量增，更有望迎來價增 :我們認為光頡的高階精密電阻供需緊張格
       局至少延續至 2027 年，除目前部分產品交期仍較過去延長數週、訂單能見度
       已達 2027 年下半年外，高規格產品具較高製程及良率門檻，新供應商短期亦
       難以補足供給。從海外同業 Vishay 近期動態亦可觀察到類似趨勢，公司 2026
       年持續推動價格調整，且部分漲價已逐步反映於財務表現，反映高階電阻供應
       緊張並非單一供應商現象，而是產業供需結構正在改變。

       在需求持續高於供給的環境下，我們認為 2027 年漲價仍具延續空間，且價格
       將逐漸成為客戶取得產能的重要條件，後續調價未必採全面性調整，而可能與
       採購量及產能配置連動。另一方面，光頡新增產能並非單純追求出貨量，而將
       優先配置至高規格、高毛利及價格接受度較高的產品，意味著公司可望同時受
       惠於 ASP 提升及產品組合優化。我們因此認為， 2027 年光頡的獲利成長除了
       來自 AI 需求與產能擴充，漲價及高階產品占比提升將是毛利率與 EPS 進一步
       上修的重要驅動力。

       評價收斂不改獲利上修趨勢，維持買進 : 我們重申光頡買進評等，並上調
       2026/2027 年 EPS 預估至 5.57 元/11.13 元，反映 AI 伺服器放量帶動高階精密
       電阻需求，及交期拉長推升漲價效益，帶動產品組合與獲利能力改善。考量漲
       價效益已逐步反映，後續獲利成長將轉由 AI 需求及產品升級驅動，我們將評
       價基準由原先 2H26～1H27 EPS 調整至 2027 年 EPS，並參考 Vishay 目前約 20
       ～25 倍本益比，將合理本益比由 30 倍下修至 20 倍。

       公司簡介

       光頡成立於 1997 年 10 月，為台灣首家同時具備薄膜/厚膜製程技術及高頻被
       動元件、模組設計開發能力的專業廠商。公司長期深耕薄膜製程技術研發與高
       頻元件整合設計，專注提供符合電子產品高頻化、小型化趨勢需求的整合型被
       動元件及高頻模組等關鍵零組件。生產基地布局涵蓋台灣與中國大陸，其中台
       灣廠區包括新竹科學園區、新竹工業區及高雄二廠、三廠，中國大陸則設有無
       錫及南通生產基地。公司主要競爭者為 Vishay、KOA、國巨(2327)、華新科(2492)
       等 。 2016 年 中國被 動元件 龍頭廣 東風 華高新 科技 策略性 入股 光頡， 目前 持 股
       約 40%，為公司最大股東，有助於強化其在中國市場的布局及產業資源整合能

                                                                                                                                                                    7 October 2026
MEMO


       3Q26 revenue: roughly in line

                                            Summary: Jentech reported September 2026 revenue of TWD3,054m (-5.3% MoM and
                                            +80.0% YoY; +47.1% YoY for 9M26), after market hours on 7 October 2026. Its 3Q26
                                            revenue of TWD9,493m (+30.5% QoQ and +87.3% YoY) accounted for a respective 98.4%
                                            and 97.4% of our and Bloomberg consensus estimates for 3Q26 revenue, respectively.

                                            We have a Buy (1) call, with a 12-month TP of TWD10,000, based on a target PER of 73x
                                            applied to our 1-year-forward EPS. For more information on the company, please refer to
                                            our latest flash note, 3Q26 preview: impressive rising ASP trend, on 29 September 2026.

                                            What’s the impact
                                            • 3Q26 revenue: roughly in line. Jentech reported September 2026 revenue of
                                              TWD3,054m (-5.3% MoM and +80.0% YoY; +47.1% YoY for 9M26). Its 3Q26 revenue of
                                              TWD9,493m (+30.5% QoQ and +87.3% YoY) accounted for a respective 98.4% and
                                              97.4% of our (TWD9,650m, +32.7% QoQ and +90.4% YoY) and Bloomberg consensus
                                              estimates for 3Q26 revenue, respectively. Revenue mix in September 2026 is: heat
                                              spreader (79.7%; +94.2% YoY), lead frame (7.8%; +47.9% YoY), electronic components
                                              (4.0%; -12.4% YoY), communications (0.7%; +53.8% YoY) and others (7.7%; +70.8%
                                              YoY); revenue mix in 3Q26 is: heat spreader (79.3%; +107.1% YoY), lead frame (7.2%;
                                              +43.0% YoY), electronic components (3.8%; -4.5% YoY), communication (0.7%; -13.5%
                                              YoY) and others (8.9%; +64.1% YoY).

                                              from removable lids in 2027, with these being implemented in Vera Rubin and Rubin

We have a Buy (1) call, with a 12-month TP of TWD10,000, based on a target PER of 73x
applied to our 1-year-forward EPS. Based on our 2026/27E EPS, the stock is currently
trading at PERs of 98.5x/38.7x, vs. its past-3-year trading range of 16-53x. Key downside
risks: weaker-than-expected global AI server demand; slower-than-expected thermal spec
upgrades.

                                                 ready in 2Q27, with production starting in 3Q27. In 2027, we expect higher revenue
                                                 contributions from ASICs and servers, as well as an increase in ASIC liquid-cooling
                                                 penetration rate (ie, 50%+ for one of ASIC client’s project in 2027 vs. 10% in 2026) to
                                                 support gross margin expansion. For 4Q26, we expect revenue momentum to
                                                 strengthen QoQ and continue into 2027.

                                               What we recommend
                                               We have a Buy (1) rating and 12-month TP of TWD4,465, based on a target PER of 30x
                                               applied to our one-year-forward EPS estimate. Based on our 2026/27E EPS, the stock is
                                               currently trading at PERs of 34.8x/23.0x, vs. its past-3-year trading range of 5-25x. Key
                                               downside risks: slower-than-expected progress in high gross-margin orders; slower AI
                                               server adoption; an economic downturn weighing on end demand.

                        Valuation
                        We set our target price at NT$1,450, based on 35x average 2027E-28E earnings. We value Yageo based on PE as we believe the
                        company’s earnings performance and industry dynamics would be the key focuses of the market. Our target multiple of 35x is
                        at the higher end of the trading range since 2022. During this period the company has gone through the cycles, successfully
                        integrated the acquired business to enhance its product offerings, and started to deliver stable margins and earnings.


                        Risks
                        Key downside risks to our target price and rating include: 1) slower-than-expected demand recovery; 2) intensified peer and
                        pricing competition; 3) execution risks associated with M&A integration and synergies; and 4) FX and interest rate fluctuations.

Company profile

  Established in 1979, Acter Group (Acter) is a leading engineering services provider specialising in
  cleanroom, electromechanical, and high-tech facility integration solutions for semiconductor,
  optoelectronics, biotech, green energy, and advanced manufacturing clients across Taiwan, China and
  the rest of the world. As of 2025, its revenue comprised cleanroom electromechanical (71%), water, gas
  and chemical delivery systems (20%), consumer industry electromechanical (4%), biomedical (2%) and
  high-tech equipment & materials sales & services (3%).

                                         Human resources are an additional limitation to capacity growth. Cleanroom
                                         engineering is highly technical and labour-intensive, relying on specialised on-site
                                         installation and supervision that cannot be replaced by robots. At the same time, the
                                         industry faces severe labour shortages and an aging workforce, and younger generations
                                         are reluctant to join field operations. Cross-border staff deployment is also less cost-
                                         efficient than local hiring.

                                         Cleanrooms involve complex system integration, creating high barriers to entry. A
                                         cleanroom construction includes 4 sequential phases, where each phase usually requires
                                         totally different areas of expertise. Therefore, the competitive landscape in each area
                                         differs. The process begins with civil & structural (C&S) works to establish the physical
                                         plant, followed by mechanical, electrical, and plumbing (MEP) works for essential utility
                                         generation, where Acter is one of the leading global experts. After MEP is finished,
                                         chemicals/gas/water are then distributed via main systems through primary piping
                                         network and finally delivered to production equipment through hook-up systems. As

                        global supply chains restructure under N+1 (domestic market + 1) strategies, companies
                        building overseas facilities in places like the US face strict and complicated licensing
                        processes, particularly on fire safety and hazardous chemicals. Without experience dealing
                        with such engineering and safety issues, construction timelines can be severely delayed.

                        As a result, even with advanced equipment and chip designs, a high-tech company cannot
                        begin production without adequate cleanroom space, skilled engineers, and system-
                        integration capabilities. Therefore, cleanroom engineering contractors hold significant
                        bargaining power and capacity allocation leverage in today's tech supply chain.

                        IC foundry
                        In the foundry sector, where the cleanroom supply-demand shortage is the tightest, project
                        activity remains centred on advanced process capacity expansion in Taiwan and Arizona.
                        Simultaneously, domestic advanced node development remains intense, with multi-phase
                        fab builds advancing across Hsinchu, Taichung, and Kaohsiung. Local cleanroom and MEP
                        integration demand is further boosted by advanced packaging facilities in Taiwan (such as
                        Chiayi and Tainan) and upcoming projects in the US are set to contribute revenue for the
                        cleanroom providers in the following years.

                        Memory
                        The memory segment is exhibiting robust momentum as well, mainly catalysed by HBM
                        capacity additions. Projects such as the plant in Japan, transitioned to contribution for the
                        cleanroom EPCM providers starting from 2026. In Taiwan, turnkey engineering contracts in
                        Miaoli are also actively underway. This trend is reinforced by stronger-than-expected
                        expansion activity from memory producers in China.

                        OSAT, PCB and ODM/OEM
                        For OSAT companies, demand is also surging due to the spill-over effect of advanced
                        packaging protocols and N+1 supply chain restructuring. The OSAT names are expanding
                        their footprint both in Southern Taiwan and in overseas locations including in the US and
                        Southeast Asia. Major engineering contracts signed between OSAT clients and Acter show
                        stable long-term workload for strong cleanroom demand over our forecast horizon.
                        Similarly, overseas expansion for PCB manufacturing is peaking in Southeast Asia,
                        especially in Thailand. We expect Chinese PCB players to also increase their capacity, just
                        like memory companies in the past year. Except for front-end and back-end chip
                        manufacturing, ODM/OEM and data centre infrastructure is also a key growth engine for
                        the EPCM industry. Major Taiwanese ODMs are building production facilities in Texas and
                        Mexico to meet local manufacturing needs. Cleanroom contractors, such as Acter,
                        providing MEP and system integration in Texas are directly benefiting from these projects.
                        The shift toward liquid cooling systems has also increased engineering complexity,
                        favouring few cleanroom companies with the expertise to deliver complex integration for
                        CSPs in both North America and Southeast Asia.

                             and hook-up systems. In China, Suzhou Winmax, also a subsidiary of Novatech, focuses

                             covers cleanroom engineering integration, water, power, chemical and gas-utility systems,
                             as well as post-completion validation and maintenance, ensuring cross-system

                             Under global supply chain diversification trends, this unified group strategy strengthens
                             order-winning capabilities in overseas markets. Clients expanding internationally face

                             A diverse client base helps Acter weather economic cycles
                             Acter’s main competitive advantage is its diversification of clients by industry and region.
                             This guides the company through the peaks and troughs of the economy, which is
                             especially crucial given the strong cyclicality of the semiconductor/high-tech industry. Acter
                             serves a broad client base across semiconductors, OSAT, PCB, electronics assembly
                             (ODM), CSP data centres, biopharmaceuticals and even the consumer industry (including
                             commercial real estate and logistics), whereas many peers rely on a few large foundry
                             clients. When semiconductor demand slows, capacity expansion in the PCB or data centre
                             sectors offset the decline. Additionally, Acter avoids concentration risk and margin
                             compression from major foundry accounts, as projects from leading foundries yield lower
                             margins; by serving niche markets like US-based CSPs, the company achieves higher
                             gross margins.

                             Geographically, Acter operates across Taiwan, China, Southeast Asia, the US and other
                             countries. The company has OSAT and foundry customers in Taiwan and China, PCB
                             clients expanding into Thailand, and ODM and data centre clients establishing operations
                             in the US. Across different countries, local hiring and local supply chain implementation
                             can further reduce costs and increase efficiency relative to peers reliant on a cross-border
                             labour force.

                             Labour shortages
                             Amid global labour shortages, Acter minimises the operational impact and turns workforce
                             constraints into a moat through localised talent development. Since engineering labour
                             cannot easily be automated, Acter has built a cross-border talent pipeline via industry-
                             academia partnerships. The company recruits Southeast Asian students for specialised
                             M&E engineering training in Taiwan, deploying them to global project sites after their
                             graduation to solve labour bottlenecks. This structure maintains an engineering team with
                             an average tenure of more than 7 years, creating an operational barrier in an industry with
                             a high employee turnover rate.

                             Compared with peers relying on high-cost personnel sent from Taiwan, we note that Acter’s
                             local hiring strategy creates cost and efficiency advantages. Prioritising compliant local
                             hiring across overseas markets reduces travel expenses while accelerating integration with
                             local supply chains and regulations. Localised teams also handle post-completion services
                             and technical support directly on-site, building long-term client trust in overseas markets.

                        Hon Precision
                        Valuation
                        Our target price of NT$11,000 is based on a target PER multiple of 36x applied to the average of our 2027E/28E EPS estimates.
                        Our PER target of 35x is set at 1-std above its 1-year PER average, justified by its high share of the AI/HPC testing handler
                        market, which we estimate could support an earnings CAGR of 77% in 2025-28, higher than its 3-year CAGR at c40% in 2022-
                        25. Our estimated 77% earning CAGR is also higher than the +40% average (Bloomberg consensus) of its global testing
                        equipment peers. As its peers have been trading at average 36x PER on 2027/28 consensus EPS in the past 1 year, we believe
                        Hon Precision deserves a further re-rating to our target PER of 36x.


                        Risks
                        Our quantitative risk rating system, which looks at historical share price volatility, rates Hon Precision High Risk. However, we
                        are not assigning a High Risk rating as we forecast an earnings CAGR of >75%, significantly stronger than the growth outlook
                        for its global peers. Also, we note its dominant position in AI/HPC handler market and expanding market TAM opportunity,
                        which support our constructive view over its growth outlook.

                        Key downside risks that could impede the shares from reaching our target price: 1) Global AI demand slowdown driving weaker
                        capacity build for semiconductor equipment; 2) unexpected share losses at its major AI projects; 3) slower-than-expected
                        capacity ramp at its new facilities, or the company taking a long time to find/secure new sites; 4) slower-than-expected
                        development of its CPO business; 5) shorter-than-expected testing time leading to lower demand for its products; 6) weak
                        adoption of high-premium cold plate products; and 7) increasing competition from new entrants.

                        Auras Technology
                        Valuation
                        We value Auras using a PE-based approach, reflecting its accelerating earnings trajectory and rising share in liquid cooling
                        market of AI servers. Our TP of NT$1,800 is based on 20x 2027E EPS, which we believe is justified given the company’s
                        expanding server revenue base, deeper engagement with CSP customers, and broader product portfolio across cold plates,
                        CDMs, and CDUs.


                        Risks
                        This stock is High Risk based upon our quantitative model, but assigning a High Risk rating is not supported in our view by
                        other qualitative factors such as rapid RVL progress and Thailand expansion, and so a High Risk rating has not been applied.
                        Key downside risks to our investment thesis and target price include: 1) slower adoption of liquid cooling; 2) heightened price
                        competition; 3) lower-than-expected share in liquid cooling components; and 4) emerging alternative cooling technologies.

Company Description
ASPEED is the world's largest baseboard management controller (BMC) chipset provider.
ASPEED introduced the first generation of server management processors in 2005. It acquired
Emulex Pilot's remote server management chip business in 2016. Besides server management
chipsets, ASPEED also produces PC/AV extension solutions and image processing system-on-
chips (SoCs). In 2023, server management chipsets accounted for 88% of total sales.


Valuation Method and Risk Statement
We derive our price target for Aspeed from PE valuation methodology relative to its historical
trading range.
We believe key upside risks for Aspeed include: 1) stronger-than-expected server demand,
particularly from hyperscalers and from AI servers with less crowding out of traditional
servers; 2) further market share expansion; 3) faster-than-expected server platform upgrades;
4) faster-than-expected progress in expanding the addressable content within servers.
We believe key downside risks for Aspeed include: 1) weaker-than-expected server demand,
particularly from hyperscalers; 2) market share losses or more intense industry competition; 3)
slower-than-expected server platform upgrades; 4) slower-than-expected progress in
expanding the addressable content within servers.

                        Valuation
                        We value AVC using a PE-based approach that factors in earnings momentum and the expansion of its addressable market.
                        Our TP of NT$4,350 is derived from applying a 25x PE multiple on 2027E EPS, which we believe is justified given the company’s
                        entrenched positioned in the server thermal segment, rising contribution from liquid cooling, and the increasing value of
                        thermal content per server as power density continues to climb. With these structural drivers still in place, we expect the
                        multiple to hold at a premium relative to its historical averages.


                        Risks
                        This stock is High Risk based upon our quantitative model but assigning a High Risk rating is not supported by other
                        qualitative factors such as cold-plate leadership and deep CSP penetration, and so a High Risk rating has not been applied.
                        Key downside risks to our investment thesis and target price include: 1) slower adoption pace for liquid cooling adoption; 2)
                        heightened price competition; 3) lower-than-expected share in liquid cooling components; and 4) emerging alternative cooling
                        technologies.

  ESG 分析

分別藉由「在 ESG 議題上的曝險」和「個別公司在 ESG 議題上的執行力」兩個面向來衡量公司於 ESG 上的表現。

► ESG 總分： 帆宣整體的 ESG 風險評級屬於低風險，於 Sustainalytics 資料庫所覆蓋的公司中排名亦排行於靠後的位置，
   但在半導體設備行業中的公司中排名微略領先同業。

► 在 ESG 議題上的曝險： 帆宣的整體曝險屬於低等水準，但略低於半導體設備行業的平均水準。公司較需要改善的 ESG
   議題包含人力資本、商業道德及資源使用等。

► 個別公司在 ESG 議題上的執行力：帆宣在針對重大 ESG 議題的管理水準和執行力屬中等。崇越於 ESG 相關揭露程度
   高，顯示其對投資人及大眾的責任感極佳，雖說公司有針對重大 ESG 議題進行管控，但對於關鍵領域仍缺乏相關政策
   及計畫。然而，目前崇越尚未涉及任何 ESG 重大爭議。

       智易科技為台灣一線網通設備廠：智易為仁寶(2324)旗下網通設備公司，專注
       於提供家庭與中小企業用戶的聯網解決方案，主要產品線分為 Mobility(行動
       通訊)、Smart Home(智慧家庭)以及 Broadband(寬頻固網)三大類，其中 Mobility
       以 5G FWA CPE 為核心，Smart Home 涵蓋 Wi‑Fi Extender、Gateway、STB 以
       及企業新產品等，Broadband 則涵蓋 Cable Modem 與 PON 等聯網設備，2Q26
       產品比重為 Mobility 38%、Smart Home 32%、Broadband 26%。地區別方面，
       北美占 61%、歐洲占 29%、亞洲占 10%，由於北美電信商資本支出強勁帶動
       5G FWA 與 Wi‑Fi 升級需求，且歐洲因地緣衝突使總體經濟疲弱、電信標案推
       進較為保守，營運重點持續轉向北美。產能布局上，公司 主 要 產 能 位於 越 南 ，
       過往中國產能已轉為供應商管理模式，印度則採外包方式進行，以分散地緣
       風險並貼近客戶區域需求。

       圖表一：智易 5G CPE 與 PON 產品


       記憶體漲價影響毛利率表現及出貨量：2026 年電子產業普遍面臨 記憶體漲價
       壓力，由於記憶體價格大幅上揚，且網通產品仍廣泛採用 DDR3/DDR4 規 格 ，
       使記憶體在網通設備 BOM 成本占比由過往不到 5%提升至 20%以上，進而對
       毛利率造成壓力。營收方面，雖然公司累計至 9 月營收持續創新高，但相對
       於記憶體漲價帶動網通產品 ASP 上揚約 20%以上，累計營收僅年增 3.34%，
       顯示出貨量實際呈衰退態勢，主因電信商客戶並未因記憶體成本上升而調高
       2026 年度採購預算，導致公司在 ASP 提升的同時出貨量下滑。我們預期記憶
       體成本在 2027 年仍難以有顯著下滑，仍需觀察客戶 2027 年採購預算是否上
       調，以及記憶體供應是否能滿足訂單需求。毛利率方面，由於 1H26 仍主要消
       化過往備貨的低價記憶體庫存，2H26 起將逐步反映高價記憶體採購成本，預
       期 2H26 毛利率將面臨較大壓力。

       新產品帶來新成長動能：智易於 2026 年逐步切入企業市場，陸續推出企業資
       安交換器與企業 Wi‑Fi Access Point 等產品，並於 1Q26 開始出貨，標誌公司
       從電信營運商與家庭用戶市場延伸至企業級應用。年底公司將進一步推出資
       料交換器(Data Switch)，預期 2027 年起開始貢獻營收，同時 2027 年亦規劃推
       出 企業 用 Router，以 完善 企業 網路 產品組 合。雖 然目 前企 業相關 營收占 比 仍
       低於 10%，但由於基期較低，預期 2027 年企業市場將成為重要成長動能之一。
       除了企業市場以外，公司在光纖與 Cable 領域亦持續推出新產品：光纖 CPE
       原先預期 3Q26 出貨，但因軟體修改與客戶驗證因素遞延至 1Q27，並於 2Q27
       起持續放量成長；Cable 產品則於 1Q26 開始出貨，惟目前量體仍小，且客戶
       並未釋出更多訂單，目前貢獻較低。

       漲價效益持續發酵，4Q26 毛利率續升 : 公司今年 5～6 月起陸續與客戶進行漲
       價協商，並依客戶、產品及訂單狀況逐步反映，且主要針對新接訂單，因此漲
       價效益並非立即反映於營收及毛利率。隨 9～10 月開始陸續 出 貨 漲價後 訂 單 ，
       產品組合持續優化，漲價效益可望逐步挹注毛利率；我們認為由於 9 月營收已
       大致反映前一波漲價，加上新增產能尚未完全開出，預期 10～11 月營收維持
       相 對 穩 定 ， 惟 產 品 組 合 持 續 優 化 ， 漲 價 效 益 仍 可 帶 動 毛 利 率 進 一 步 提 升 。 12
       月營收則仍將受到年度盤點及聖誕假期等季節性因素影響而略有波動，但在高
       毛利產品占比提升及漲價效益持續發酵下，獲利率可望維持高檔，因此我們上
       調 4Q26 營收至 11.1 億元，毛利率至 41.89%，EPS 為 2.1 元。

       2027 年不只量增，更有望迎來價增 :我們認為光頡的高階精密電阻供需緊張格
       局至少延續至 2027 年，除目前部分產品交期仍較過去延長數週、訂單能見度
       已達 2027 年下半年外，高規格產品具較高製程及良率門檻，新供應商短期亦
       難以補足供給。從海外同業 Vishay 近期動態亦可觀察到類似趨勢，公司 2026
       年持續推動價格調整，且部分漲價已逐步反映於財務表現，反映高階電阻供應
       緊張並非單一供應商現象，而是產業供需結構正在改變。

       在需求持續高於供給的環境下，我們認為 2027 年漲價仍具延續空間，且價格
       將逐漸成為客戶取得產能的重要條件，後續調價未必採全面性調整，而可能與
       採購量及產能配置連動。另一方面，光頡新增產能並非單純追求出貨量，而將
       優先配置至高規格、高毛利及價格接受度較高的產品，意味著公司可望同時受
       惠於 ASP 提升及產品組合優化。我們因此認為， 2027 年光頡的獲利成長除了
       來自 AI 需求與產能擴充，漲價及高階產品占比提升將是毛利率與 EPS 進一步
       上修的重要驅動力。

       評價收斂不改獲利上修趨勢，維持買進 : 我們重申光頡買進評等，並上調
       2026/2027 年 EPS 預估至 5.57 元/11.13 元，反映 AI 伺服器放量帶動高階精密
       電阻需求，及交期拉長推升漲價效益，帶動產品組合與獲利能力改善。考量漲
       價效益已逐步反映，後續獲利成長將轉由 AI 需求及產品升級驅動，我們將評
       價基準由原先 2H26～1H27 EPS 調整至 2027 年 EPS，並參考 Vishay 目前約 20
       ～25 倍本益比，將合理本益比由 30 倍下修至 20 倍。

Zhen Ding Technology (4958.TW)

New businesses taking off; Buy

CITI’S TAKE

Zhen Ding’s (ZDT) AI infra business (server/optical/substrate) is tracking better-than-expected YTD. These businesses all carry high GM profiles of >30% vs consumer electronics products’ of 20-25%, which bodes well for ZDT’s profitability growth in 2027. Looking into 2H26, we expect AI infra business to bear more fruit and would help mitigate the season impact in 1Q27, especially for the bottom line. Meanwhile, given HDI/mSAP capacity supply tightness, we observe that Apple suppliers show less willingness to support iPhone/Mac demand, which would help increase ZDT’s bargaining power in consumer electronics products. We raise our 2027/28E earnings forecasts to factor in fast-growing AI infra business and lift our TP to NT$750 (27x 2027E EPS) from NT$600 (25x 2027E EPS), as we sense that the market views ZDT more as an ABF substrate maker. Buy.

3Q26 results preview: GM of 25-26% — We forecast 3Q26E GM of 25.6% (+2.5ppt QoQ) vs consensus forecast of 25.2%, supported by high-season for iPhone, ABF/BT and optical module which more than offset rising depreciation burden from initial ramp of HDI capacity for AI server business in 2H26. AI infra business (server/optical/substrate) accounted for 23% of total 1H26 sales already (vs 21.6% in 1H26), which is tracking well and would likely reach 25% in 2026. We expect AI infra business to gain more traction from 3Q26E onward till 4Q27E, helping mitigate the seasonality difference in 1H/2H. Meanwhile, the management thinks AI infra sales mix could reach 30%/45-50% in 2027/28 which is far ahead of its initial target reaching 45-50% mix by 2030. We expect 4Q26E GM to further improve to 26.1% (+0.5ppt QoQ), close to historical peak levels.

ABF/BT substrate: 2027/28 capacity fully sold out — As with other ABF peers, ZDT’s ABF capacity in 2027/28 has been fully sold out. We expect Nvidia, Mediatek and likely an AI ASIC project will be the key drivers to its ABF business, along with China AI demand till 2030. As per the management, US customers would likely account for up to 70% of its ABF sales next year vs 50% in the past. The company’s current ABF capacity expansion is ramp-up of one new fab in China every year till 2030. For BT substrate, the company would pause its capacity expansion and enhance its product mix first. Considering other BT peers’ recent price hike action and improving S/D status, we expect its BT UR/GM to further improve. In our view, mid-term ABF/BT GM profile of 45-50%/30-35% in 2H27 is achievable for ZDT. We currently forecast 94%/105%/57% sales growth in its ABF+BT segment in 2026/27/28E.

Buy

                                 About the PCIe migration and Gen6 spec upgrade
   PCIe has been used in on-     PCIe has long been used for on-board and in-chassis interconnects. In the Vera
        board and in-chassis     Rubin platform, PCIe Gen6 serves as the in-tray bridge to front-of-tray modules
              interconnects      such as CX-9 SuperNICs, BlueField-4 DPUs and NVMe storage. GPU-to-GPU scale-
                                 up runs on NVLink, with UALink as the open alternative; these fabrics work
                                 alongside PCIe.

                                 In order to address ever-larger training models, the PCIe must scale with the fast-
                                 growing size of model parameters and datasets. The move from Gen5 to Gen6 is
                                 not a simple speed doubling, even though per-lane bandwidth rises from 32 GT/s
                                 to 64 GT/s. It reworks the link from the coding scheme up. Gen1 through Gen5
                                 doubled I/O speed using NRZ signaling. Gen6 switches to PAM4 four-level
                                 signaling and, for the first time, adds FEC (Forward Error Correction), which lets the
                                 receiver detect and correct transmission errors on its own.

    Each generation upgrade      Each generation doubles bandwidth while tightening signal-integrity specs, which
      raises barriers to entry   demands higher-precision connector manufacturing. This creates a real barrier to
                                 entry for high-speed connector suppliers.

                 Key risks
                 We see four key operational risks for ACES:

                 Raw material cost volatility: Copper prices drive a large share of Cogs for ACES's
                 cable products, while connectors carry far less exposure. ACES currently reprices
                 its cable products with customers on a quarterly basis, which has allowed it to
                 sustain a long-term GM of around 20% on power cables. However, the pass-through
                 might be lagging, so sharp copper price swings could cause quarterly GM to
                 fluctuate before repricing impact catches up.

                 Delays in ODM pull-in: ACES ships its high-speed connectors directly to ODM
                 customers. Because rack assembly sits at the final stage of the AI server supply
                 chain, any upstream disruption, such as components shortages and assembly yield
                 issue, could push out rack shipment schedules or reduce volumes. This could in turn
                 lead ODMs to cut or defer orders for high-speed connectors from ACES, creating
                 quarter-to-quarter volatility in server revenue.

                 Slower-than-expected ramp-up at Bloom Energy: Power cables for Bloom will
                 account for 28%/35% of ACES's revenue in 2027/28SP, which makes Bloom's
                 ramp-up the single largest swing factor in our forecasts. Delays could arise on both
                 the supply and demand sides. On the supply side, Bloom could fall behind its
                 capacity plan if new facility fit-out, equipment installation or hiring takes longer
                 than expected. On the demand side, its datacentre customers could defer
                 deployments due to grid interconnection, gas supply or financing hurdles, or due to
                 regulatory headwinds such as tighter permitting and emissions rules for on-site gas-
                 fired generation, utility restrictions on behind-the-meter power, or changes to fuel
                 cell tax incentives. Either scenario would directly reduce ACES's power cable
                 shipments. As volumes scale, Bloom may also qualify a second cable supplier, which
                 would add pressure to ACES's share and ASP.

                 Prolonged NB weakness: NB and Consumer remains ACES's largest segment at 35%
                 of 2026SP revenue, and our forecasts assume it returns to 4%/12% growth in
                 2027/28SP on a Windows 12-driven replacement cycle. If end-demand stays soft
                 or the replacement cycle slips, a further NB decline could offset part of the growth
                 from Bloom and AI servers and dilute group GM.

                 Investment thesis
                 ACES is evolving from a notebook connector maker into a supplier of AI
                 interconnects and power cables, with two growth engines ramping at the same
                 time. The first is Bloom Energy. ACES has co-developed SOFC power cables with
                 Bloom for about six years, and it is currently one of three suppliers of Bloom's power
                 cable assemblies, with around one-third of the total. It ships inner PCS and hot-box
                 cables in 2026 and adds external DLO high-voltage cables from 2027, with order
                 visibility extending to 2028 and beyond. The second engine is AI/ASIC servers. On
                 ASIC platforms, ODMs have more say in supplier selection, so ACES wins both
                 motherboard and daughterboard sockets, which lifts content from 10-20 to ~30
                 units per rack. Gen6 raises connector ASP by ~15%, and a new in-chassis PCIe Gen6
                 cable line, qualified by two CSPs, adds a higher-content stream. ACES integrates
                 vertically from wire drawing to final assembly, which makes it one of the few
                 Taiwanese suppliers able to ship connector-plus-cable solutions as CSPs
                 consolidate their vendor base.

                 Catalysts
                 (1) Bloom's capacity ramp from 2GW to 4GW/6GW in 2026-28 and new data-
                 center wins (Oracle, Nebius, AEP, Equinix) converting into cable orders; (2) DLO
                 high-voltage cable shipments starting in 2027; (3) ASIC customer ramps in 2H26
                 and a broader product range beyond MCIO into Multi-Track, board-to-board and
                 E1/E3 connectors; (4) rising Gen6 penetration on AI server trays; (5) high-speed
                 cable lines expanding from two to eight by end-2026, with GM improving from
                 ~20% toward ~30%.

                 Valuation details
                 We adopt a PE-based valuation methodology as we believe the market will mainly
                 focus on the earnings growth outlooks of high-speed connector makers, which is
                 better reflected with PE metrics. We assign a target multiple of 20x PE, more than
                 +1sd of the three-year average, to reflect a strong outlook with margin expansion
                 and an EPS Cagr of 72% in 2026-28 on solid Bloom Energy demand and increasing
                 high speed connector content.

                 Investment risks
                 There could be downside risk to sales growth and margins if: (1) Bloom's
                 deployments or backlog conversion slow on financing, gas supply or permitting
                 delays, or ACES loses share among Bloom's cable suppliers; (2) ASIC programs ramp
                 more slowly or CSP Capex is cut; (3) Gen6 adoption is slower than expected, or
                 competition from Amphenol, TE, Molex and Lotes pressures ASP; (4) high-speed
                 cable yield and GM improve more slowly than we assume; (5) NB and consumer
                 demand weakens further on component shortages, tariffs and inflation; (6) TWD
                 appreciation or higher copper prices squeeze margins.

                  Investment thesis
                  Kaori is well positioned to capitalise on rising demand for liquid cooling, and it
                  expects related product shipments to ramp up. The fuel-cell business should be a
                  huge growth driver in 2026-27 to meet AI power infrastructure demand in the US.
                  In the longer term, we believe the company will also benefit from heat-pump
                  demand as Europe is phasing out gas boilers, despite some noise about near-term
                  demand. Kaori has been planning capacity expansion earlier than peers to fully
                  capture demand, with rising exposure to large clients. We thus expect the company
                  to enjoy robust earnings in coming years.

                 Catalysts
                 The major growth catalysts largely depend on fuel-cell projects for AI datacentres
                 taking off, increasing content value in liquid cooling offerings, and a clearer outlook
                 for hydrogen electrolyzer development.

                 Valuation details
                 We adopt a PE-based valuation methodology as we believe the market will mainly
                 focus on the earnings growth outlook, which is better reflected with PE metrics.
                 We base our valuation on 40x PE, which is around +1sd of its five-year average and
                 supported by an 93% EPS Cagr in 2026-28SP, to account for the surging demand
                 for AI server liquid cooling and power infrastructure. We are positive on the
                 company's long-term outlook given its growing stationary fuel cell demand from AI
                 datacentres, as well as its efforts to diversify customer exposure for liquid cooling
                 business. We believe the company can maintain its competitive edge over other
                 cooling players given its expertise in vacuum welding technology to manufacture
                 high-quality products.

                 Investment risks
                 Downside risks: 1) increased competition for Bloom Energy's fuel cell business or
                 new technology solutions replacing fuel cells; 2) slower kick-off of new fuel cell
                 projects for AI datacentres; 3) weaker-than-expected liquid cooling adoption; 4)
                 slower rollout of Europe/US government subsidies for heat pump installations.

AI驅動高速互聯，矽光子落地，CPO續章


    福邦投顧 研究部
      2026/09
 結論
⚫ AI算力需求推升高速光互聯市場。美國四大CSP持續擴大AI資料中心建置，為帶動高速光
  模組需求成長的主要動能。現階段高速光模組出貨仍以800G為主，1.6T預計自2027年逐步
  放量，也帶動矽光(SiPh)模組滲透率提高。

⚫ 矽光模組非新興產品，外型仍沿用既有可插拔光模組規格，但相較傳統光模組，SiPh具備
  元件高度整合及晶圓級量產優勢，隨高速傳輸所需而獲廣泛採用。然而，雷射晶片受限於
  上游InP基板缺貨而供應吃緊。為確保貨源，部分業者已透過長約或預付款方式鎖定供應，
  使掌握貨源者在市場上更具競爭優勢。

⚫ CPO現階段仍面臨光耦合、測試與量產等製程挑戰；對CSP而言，CPO改變其既有可插拔光
  模組的維修與更換模式，加上NPO、XPO等替代架構持續發展，使CPO雖已進入量產階段
  ，短期滲透率仍偏低。展望未來，傳輸頻寬持續提升，為降低傳輸損耗與功率，光引擎將
  逐步靠近交換器ASIC或加速卡，CPO仍具導入需求。此外，NVIDIA持續擴大NVLink
  Fusion生態系，擴大CPO潛在應用市場，惟規模部署時程仍待帶動頻寬需求的新應用興起。

⚫ 相關個股：聯亞(3081)、IET-KY(4971)、寰宇-KY(4991)、聯鈞(3450)、訊芯-KY(6451)、華
  星光(4979)、光聖(6442)、波若威(3163)、上詮(3363)、大立光(3008)

 AI算力需求推升高速光互聯市場
 AI DC建置，光通訊需求持續成長
•   生成式AI浪潮帶動美國CSP進入DC建置競賽，2023年仍為投資初期，2024年CapEx明顯加速
    ，預期2026年美國四大CSP—Amazon、Google、微軟、Meta ，CapEx合計增至7,500億美元，
    帶動高速光互聯(networking)需求。

•   Amazon更指出，預期AWS算力供不應求情況將延續至2027年，且2028年需求能見度已高。

•   2022年底ChatGPT推出帶動生成式AI浪潮，惟當時COVID-19疫情剛結束，Amazon和Meta因
    疫情期間大幅擴張基礎建設而下調2023年CapEx，使四大CSP整體CapEx較2022年略低。

 預估2031年光模組市場營收將達1,120億美元
•   市調機構預估，至2031年光模組市場營收將達1,120億美元，CAGR成長30%。AI DC為營收
    貢獻主力， 佔比達9成。

•   2025年合計資料中心與電信商的光模組營收為230億美元，當時兩者營收分別為180億與50億
    美元，差異有限；2031年資料中心的光模組營收達1,010億，電信商僅增為110億美元。


                    圖2、2025與2031年光模組市場規模比較

 光互連應用由機櫃延伸至跨資料中心
•   目前光通訊產品出貨集中於Scale Up與Scale Out應用；隨資料中心建置規模擴大及耗電量增加
    ，受限於電力與土地供給，資料中心朝分散式建置發展，並透過光纖串聯多座資料中心以進行
    共同運算，帶動Scale Across需求。

•   Scale Up為機櫃內元件與設備互連；Scale Out為資料中心內不同機櫃間互連；Scale Across為
    資料中心互連。

                 圖3、資料中心Scale Up、Scale Out與Scale Across架構


    【僅供內部教育訓練使用，嚴禁外流】                                   資料來源：Ciena, 福邦投顧彙整   7
 依傳輸距離採用不同光互聯技術
•   Scale Up傳輸距離較短，以成本較低的主動銅纜(ACC)為主；隨傳輸速率增加，銅線難以維
                                          AOC
    持訊號品質，便會採用光纖兩端配置光收發模組的主動光纜(AOC)。

•   Scale Out主流採用IMDD可插拔(pluggable)光模組。

•   NPO和CPO為應用於Scale Out和Scale up的新技術，藉縮短光引擎與交換器ASIC距離以降低
    高速傳輸的電訊號損耗。NPO的光引擎鄰近交換器ASIC擺放；CPO的光引擎與交換器ASIC
    共同封裝。

•   Scale Across傳輸距離約20公里以上，需採用相干光(coherent)技術來維持訊號品質，供應商
    相對有限，以歐美系業者為主。

                        圖4、三類架構的光互聯技術需求

 矽光子技術與供應鏈發展
 AI資料中心的光互聯台廠供應鏈
•   AI DC 高速互連升級，帶動 AOC/ACC 與800G/1.6T可插拔光模組需求成長，並推升矽光
    (SiPh)模組滲透率。台廠AOC供應商包括佳必琪與源傑。

•   台廠受惠範圍由光模組元件與封裝，進一步延伸至CW Laser、光學次模組封裝及 PIC 代工

•   高密度光纖佈線需求同步增加，帶動 MPO/Jumper、Fiber Harness、Shuffle Module 等產品需
    求，台廠供應商包括光聖、波若威、佳必琪、貿聯-KY。

 光模組朝高速與高密度整合演進
•    AI DC帶動高速光模組需求，2026年以400G、800G為主，1.6T開始放量；2027年1.6T出貨量
     將明顯提升，並預期2028年導入3.2T。市調機構LightCounting預估，隨800G、1.6T等高速光
     模組需求增加，矽光模組滲透率將提升，2026年矽光模組銷售額YoY成長110%，占整體光模
     組市場約50%。
•    光模組速率提升是透過增加光通道或提高單通道速率來實現，以每通道200G為例，800G需4
     個光通道，1.6T則增至8個，通道數增加所需的調變器、PD等元件數量也隨之增加，使耦合
     及封裝複雜度提高，凸顯矽光模組的整合優勢

 矽光PIC高度整合光元件並以半導體製程量產
•    矽光模組是指搭載矽光PIC的光模組，矽光PIC透過半導體製程，將調變器、波導等光學功能
     整合於晶片，減少離散元件組裝及光學對準步驟，並有利於晶圓級量產。
•    2016年英特爾即推出矽光子光模組，惟早期高速傳輸需求有限，矽光PIC整合效益尚不顯著；
     隨800G、1.6T以上高速光模組放量，通道數及光元件數量增加，矽光PIC整合優勢浮現。
•    現階段矽光模組仍沿用沿用OSFP、QSFP-DD既有可插拔光模組外型。
•    過去光通訊PIC多採III-V族材料，雷射與光元件可單晶整合，但市場規模較小且製程專用，多
     以IDM方式生產；矽光PIC採CMOS相容製程，可導入成熟矽晶圓代工模式，實現規模量產與
     降低成本，然無法與雷射整合。

 矽光PIC需求擴大，專業分工成形
•   矽光PIC晶圓代工目前以Tower半導體量產規模及客戶能見度最高；聯電亦積極切入，2025年
    取得比利時半導體研究機構imec的12吋矽光子製程技術授權，2026年於新加坡12吋廠量產
    1.6T PIC，預計2027年向更多客戶開放矽光代工平台。

•   除英特爾外，其餘具備矽光PIC設計能力業者並未單獨銷售PIC，而是將PIC與EIC、DSP整合
    為光引擎(optical engine)後出售。

•   2023年英特爾出售光模組事業予Jabil，專注於提供整合雷射的矽光PIC。

 雷射供應鏈呈IDM與專業分工並存
•   Lumentum、Cohernet、博通採IDM模式，具備從LD設計、磊晶、晶圓製程至雷射封裝能力，
    並視產能與產品需求委外，如Coherent將部分LD封裝委由聯鈞生產。

•   磊晶製程方面，全新、聯亞採用MOCVD設備，英特磊以MBE為主，IQE同時具備MOCVD與

 CPO發展趨勢與導入挑戰
 CPO於3.2T世代有望加速滲透
•   台積電表示CPO模組將於2026年下半年量產，惟依供應鏈資訊，初期出貨量仍低、市場規模
    有限。市調機構預估，CPO光模組出貨量將自2027年起明顯成長，2030年達約6,000萬顆；
    滲透率部分，將由2027年的11%提升至2028年的19%，2030年進一步達38%。

•   業界普遍認為，傳輸速率進入3.2T世代後，CPO在功耗與頻寬密度上的優勢將更為明顯。博

 CPO推動光電共封裝，FAU成光耦合關鍵元件
•   CPO為光電共封裝架構，將 PIC與EIC 整合為光引擎(OE)，再與Switch ASIC共封裝於同一載
    板，目標降低電訊號傳輸距離與功耗。

•   雷射仍放置於交換器機箱前面板，且維持可插拔，以方便更換。

•   目前台積電以COUPE平台整合PIC與EIC成光引擎，然提高光耦合效率、降低光進入 PIC 的
    損耗，成為CPO主要瓶頸之一，也使 FAU 成為關鍵元件。

                                    圖11、CPO主要元件

    光引擎(OE)        外部雷射       光纖陣列
                    (ELS)      單元
      PIC

                                  FAU
      EIC
                    矽光模組
              雷射

                                        維持可插拔(b)。


    【僅供內部教育訓練使用，嚴禁外流】                              資料來源：Photonics Spectra, 福邦投顧彙整 20
 FAU難以晶片化，攸關CPO光耦合效率與量產時程
•   目前台積電COUPE平台優先採用光柵(grating)耦合架構，FAU以黏膠固定於光學引擎上
    方。光線平行射出，需以反射鏡導入PIC；COUPE端利用矽透鏡將光聚焦至光柵耦合器
    ，也配置金屬反射鏡回收散射光，提升光耦合效率。
•   光耦合效率攸關光學元件設計與光纖精密對位。FAU除涉及光學設計外，光纖亦需精準
    置入V-groove，並完成固定、端面研磨與對位封裝，工序繁雜而被視為CPO規模量產瓶
    頸之一。
•   FAU投入業者主要包括線材廠、傳統FAU業者及光學元件廠。例如，光聖旗下合聖推出
    以Metalens搭配反射鏡的可拆卸式FAU；大立光則推出配置80顆微型鏡頭、整合反射鏡
    與稜鏡功能的PMLA，並進一步布局多層堆疊光纖。線材廠方面，以波若威、佳必琪與
    貿聯為代表；傳統FAU業者則以上銓為代表。
                        圖12、TSMC COUPE的FAU光耦合架構


                                        大立光、合聖針對反射鏡推出解決方案


    【僅供內部教育訓練使用，嚴禁外流】                             資料來源：TSMC, 福邦投顧彙整 21
 FAU技術升級聚焦提升耦光效率與縮短對位時間
•   FAU主要發展方向為可拆卸設計、多層光纖堆疊與被動對位。其中，可拆卸式方案以美、日
    業者布局較積極，主要考量FAU或光纖生損壞可直接更換，避免拆除整組光學引擎，降低維
    修難度及交換器損壞風險。

•   目前FAU多採主動對位，透過反覆微調位置並量測光功率，找出最佳耦合點後固定，雖可補
    償製造與組裝誤差，但組裝時間長。被動對位仰賴高精度製程與定位結構，將精度要求前移
    ，以簡化後段組裝並提升量產效率

                     圖13、FAU正發展可拆卸、多層堆疊及被動對準

    日商Senko的可拆卸FAU


                     Teramount雙層光纖設計使
                     光纖量從單層的32條增為       Teramount與高塔半導體合作開發Bump-ready wafer，
                     64條。               即在PIC晶圓階段預先製作光學耦合與對位結構。

 NPO持續演進 成為Scale Up另一選擇
•   NPO被視為CPO折衷方案，光引擎置於鄰近交換器ASIC，降低傳輸損耗且保留維修彈性。

•   華為認為NPO具備提供400G/lane的潛力，3.2T世代未必需全面導入CPO。

•   博通、Marvell、Coherent皆已展示或推出NPO方案，光源架構部分，Marvell主打無DSP、配
    置CW雷射；博通展示VCSEL方案，Coherent同時推出VCSEL和CW方案，VCSEL功耗低，
    晶片尺寸小，可高密度排列，並與光引擎整合封裝，然傳輸距離有限，適合Scale-up應用。

•   被視為Marvell合作業者的華星光，預期2027年下半開始量產1.6T NPO模組，2028年出貨量
    體將較為顯著。

                        圖14、NPO與CPO技術路徑比較

                NPO                               CPO
                                            光引擎
          光引擎                                           外部雷射


       光引擎鄰近ASIC擺放。                光引擎與ASIC置於同一載板，配置外部雷射。


    【僅供內部教育訓練使用，嚴禁外流】                             資料來源：華為, 福邦投顧彙整 23
 XPO重塑可插拔模組 挑戰CPO的Scale Out市場
•   美網通業者Arista於2026年成立XPO MSA，並展示首代支援200G/lane，頻寬12.8T的可插拔
    XPO模組，後續將發展400G/lane、單模組頻寬25.6T，惟量產與規模商用時程尚未明朗。
    XPO MSA成員橫跨CSP、ASIC、光元件與光模組供應鏈，包括微軟、Marvell、Coherent、
    Lumentum及新易盛等。Arista為Ethernet交換器設備商，主導XPO規格與生態系發展。

•   XPO主打Scale-out應用，強調單一XPO模組可取代8顆OSFP，在有限機箱空間內提高整體傳
    輸頻寬。由於XPO採全新模組機構，交換器須配合重新設計供電、散熱及相關介面，目前規
    格制定與系統平台仍以Arista為主；儘管XPO MSA讓CSP在光模組供應商選擇上更具彈性，
    但在其他交換器業者尚未跟進前，導入XPO亦可能意味對Arista交換器平台的更高依賴。

                        圖15、XPO模組架構與應用示意

                                            頻寬至12.8T

 Open CPX以標準化介面挑戰NVIDIA封閉式CPO架構
•   美系光傳輸設備商Ciena與Coherent，以及連接器業者Molex、Samtec推動Open CPX MSA，
    透過標準介面讓讓光引擎可拆卸，獨立於ASIC，提高光引擎與ASIC的選擇彈性。

•   Open CPX強調架構選擇彈性，CSP可依系統需求採用NPO或CPO，雷射可選外部雷射或整合
    式雷射方案。

•   Ciena已推出採Open CPX架構的光引擎Vesta，，並以16 顆6.4T光引擎打造總頻寬102.4T的系
    統。Ciena於3Q26法說表示，Vesta樣品已售出，預計2027年開始貢獻營收、2028年放量。

               圖16、Open CPX採可拆卸光引擎設計，提升供應商選擇彈性


                                               強調光模組配置支援CPX

    【僅供內部教育訓練使用，嚴禁外流】                         資料來源：Ciena，福邦投顧彙整 25
 各種光互聯架構重塑供應鏈價值分配
•   CPO和NPO的供應鏈差異有限，皆由交換器ASIC或加速卡業者主導系統架構，光引擎、雷
    射、FAU、連接器等供應鏈皆配合設計。若CPO滲透率提高，將壓縮傳統可插拔光模組需求
    ，但具雷射組裝能力的業者仍可供應外部雷射
•   CPO的光耦合效率需求提高，使FAU重要性提升。
•   XPO藉提高模組頻寬，延續可插拔方案在高速傳輸的生命週期。
•   Open CPX採用標準介面實現光引擎可拆卸，由於PCB板端需配置CPX連接器，使連接器重
    要性提升。
•   不論採用何種光互連架構，隨AI資料中心傳輸頻寬與光路數持續增加，高密度佈線需求均將
    提升，帶動fiber jumper、fiber harness及fiber shuffle需求，如光聖已切入Google資料中心光纖
    連接供應鏈將明顯受惠。

       Open CPX   可拆卸光引擎、連接器、雷射、FAU            封閉式CPO供應鏈

    【僅供內部教育訓練使用，嚴禁外流】                                   資料來源：福邦投顧彙整 26
 CPO長期具導入需求，惟時程仍具不確定性
•   CPO在Scale-out面臨傳統可插拔光模組、XPO與NPO等架構競爭；相較下，台積電認為CPO
    在Scale-up更能發揮高頻寬、低功耗與短距離互連優勢，朝Optical I/O發展。

•   Scale-up 架構目前存在技術路線分歧—Narrow & Fast 與 Wide & Slow；前者持續提高單通道
    速率，以NVIDIA為代表，後者增加道數來擴充頻寬，微軟MOSAIC為較典型方案。

•   展望未來，儘管CPO導入時程受系統架構與成本效益影響，但隨運算規模持續擴大，銅互連
    瓶頸將推動光引擎進一步靠近交換器ASIC或XPU，CPO長期導入趨勢不變。 再者，NVIDIA
    亦透過NVLink Fusion持續擴大Fabric生態系，使採用客製XPU的業者仍可導入NVLink架構
    ，擴大CPO潛在應用市場。

                                 About the PCIe migration and Gen6 spec upgrade
   PCIe has been used in on-     PCIe has long been used for on-board and in-chassis interconnects. In the Vera
        board and in-chassis     Rubin platform, PCIe Gen6 serves as the in-tray bridge to front-of-tray modules
              interconnects      such as CX-9 SuperNICs, BlueField-4 DPUs and NVMe storage. GPU-to-GPU scale-
                                 up runs on NVLink, with UALink as the open alternative; these fabrics work
                                 alongside PCIe.

                                 In order to address ever-larger training models, the PCIe must scale with the fast-
                                 growing size of model parameters and datasets. The move from Gen5 to Gen6 is
                                 not a simple speed doubling, even though per-lane bandwidth rises from 32 GT/s
                                 to 64 GT/s. It reworks the link from the coding scheme up. Gen1 through Gen5
                                 doubled I/O speed using NRZ signaling. Gen6 switches to PAM4 four-level
                                 signaling and, for the first time, adds FEC (Forward Error Correction), which lets the
                                 receiver detect and correct transmission errors on its own.

    Each generation upgrade      Each generation doubles bandwidth while tightening signal-integrity specs, which
      raises barriers to entry   demands higher-precision connector manufacturing. This creates a real barrier to
                                 entry for high-speed connector suppliers.

                                    Industrial: a steady UPS-driven base
                                    ACES supplies industrial power cords, used mainly in uninterruptible power systems
                                    (UPS). A UPS is an electrical device that acts as a reliable buffer when the main
                                    power supply behaves abnormally, such as during a fault, outage, or unstable
                                    voltage. It keeps automation controllers, sensors, and actuators continuously
                                    powered so equipment keeps running. When a power problem occurs, the UPS
                                    supplies stable backup power to prevent equipment failure, data corruption, or
                                    system crashes. We expect ACES’s industrial business to grow steadily, with growth
                                    of 9% and 14% in 2026 and 2027, respectively.

                                    Company profile
                                    ACES was founded in 1996, and it mainly produces connectors, micro-coaxial cable,
                                    high-speed transmission cables, and RF connectors. Connectors and cable
                                    assemblies link two separate subsystems or operating units and carry the signals
                                    between them, allowing the overall system to function properly. They are used
                                    across a wide range of electronic products, with main applications spanning
                                    notebooks and PC peripherals, consumer electronics, automotive electronics, cloud
                                    servers, networking equipment, and industrial equipment.

                                    To keep pace with the push towards lighter, thinner, and smaller notebooks and
                                    consumer devices, ACES developed high-temperature-resistant, fine-pitch, and
                                    low-profile products at an early stage. At the same time, it is moving actively into
                                    the high-frequency, high-speed connectors, high-speed cables, and power supplies
                                    required for cloud servers, as well as the connector and cable assemblies used in
                                    automotive electronics.

                 Key risks
                 We see four key operational risks for ACES:

                 Raw material cost volatility: Copper prices drive a large share of Cogs for ACES's
                 cable products, while connectors carry far less exposure. ACES currently reprices
                 its cable products with customers on a quarterly basis, which has allowed it to
                 sustain a long-term GM of around 20% on power cables. However, the pass-through
                 might be lagging, so sharp copper price swings could cause quarterly GM to
                 fluctuate before repricing impact catches up.

                 Delays in ODM pull-in: ACES ships its high-speed connectors directly to ODM
                 customers. Because rack assembly sits at the final stage of the AI server supply
                 chain, any upstream disruption, such as components shortages and assembly yield
                 issue, could push out rack shipment schedules or reduce volumes. This could in turn
                 lead ODMs to cut or defer orders for high-speed connectors from ACES, creating
                 quarter-to-quarter volatility in server revenue.

                 Slower-than-expected ramp-up at Bloom Energy: Power cables for Bloom will
                 account for 28%/35% of ACES's revenue in 2027/28SP, which makes Bloom's
                 ramp-up the single largest swing factor in our forecasts. Delays could arise on both
                 the supply and demand sides. On the supply side, Bloom could fall behind its
                 capacity plan if new facility fit-out, equipment installation or hiring takes longer
                 than expected. On the demand side, its datacentre customers could defer
                 deployments due to grid interconnection, gas supply or financing hurdles, or due to
                 regulatory headwinds such as tighter permitting and emissions rules for on-site gas-
                 fired generation, utility restrictions on behind-the-meter power, or changes to fuel
                 cell tax incentives. Either scenario would directly reduce ACES's power cable
                 shipments. As volumes scale, Bloom may also qualify a second cable supplier, which
                 would add pressure to ACES's share and ASP.

                 Prolonged NB weakness: NB and Consumer remains ACES's largest segment at 35%
                 of 2026SP revenue, and our forecasts assume it returns to 4%/12% growth in
                 2027/28SP on a Windows 12-driven replacement cycle. If end-demand stays soft
                 or the replacement cycle slips, a further NB decline could offset part of the growth
                 from Bloom and AI servers and dilute group GM.

                 Investment thesis
                 ACES is evolving from a notebook connector maker into a supplier of AI
                 interconnects and power cables, with two growth engines ramping at the same
                 time. The first is Bloom Energy. ACES has co-developed SOFC power cables with
                 Bloom for about six years, and it is currently one of three suppliers of Bloom's power
                 cable assemblies, with around one-third of the total. It ships inner PCS and hot-box
                 cables in 2026 and adds external DLO high-voltage cables from 2027, with order
                 visibility extending to 2028 and beyond. The second engine is AI/ASIC servers. On
                 ASIC platforms, ODMs have more say in supplier selection, so ACES wins both
                 motherboard and daughterboard sockets, which lifts content from 10-20 to ~30
                 units per rack. Gen6 raises connector ASP by ~15%, and a new in-chassis PCIe Gen6
                 cable line, qualified by two CSPs, adds a higher-content stream. ACES integrates
                 vertically from wire drawing to final assembly, which makes it one of the few
                 Taiwanese suppliers able to ship connector-plus-cable solutions as CSPs
                 consolidate their vendor base.

                 Catalysts
                 (1) Bloom's capacity ramp from 2GW to 4GW/6GW in 2026-28 and new data-
                 center wins (Oracle, Nebius, AEP, Equinix) converting into cable orders; (2) DLO
                 high-voltage cable shipments starting in 2027; (3) ASIC customer ramps in 2H26
                 and a broader product range beyond MCIO into Multi-Track, board-to-board and
                 E1/E3 connectors; (4) rising Gen6 penetration on AI server trays; (5) high-speed
                 cable lines expanding from two to eight by end-2026, with GM improving from
                 ~20% toward ~30%.

                 Valuation details
                 We adopt a PE-based valuation methodology as we believe the market will mainly
                 focus on the earnings growth outlooks of high-speed connector makers, which is
                 better reflected with PE metrics. We assign a target multiple of 20x PE, more than
                 +1sd of the three-year average, to reflect a strong outlook with margin expansion
                 and an EPS Cagr of 72% in 2026-28 on solid Bloom Energy demand and increasing
                 high speed connector content.

                 Investment risks
                 There could be downside risk to sales growth and margins if: (1) Bloom's
                 deployments or backlog conversion slow on financing, gas supply or permitting
                 delays, or ACES loses share among Bloom's cable suppliers; (2) ASIC programs ramp
                 more slowly or CSP Capex is cut; (3) Gen6 adoption is slower than expected, or
                 competition from Amphenol, TE, Molex and Lotes pressures ASP; (4) high-speed
                 cable yield and GM improve more slowly than we assume; (5) NB and consumer
                 demand weakens further on component shortages, tariffs and inflation; (6) TWD
                 appreciation or higher copper prices squeeze margins.

AI從算力荒到晶圓荒，矽晶圓漲價循環起跑


       福邦投顧研究部
        2026/09
 目錄


     一   矽晶圓為寡占、高壁壘的上游材料   5


     二   矽晶圓因AI重寫需求曲線      16


     三   供需缺口改善，漲價循環已啟動    22


     四   相關個股              30


【僅供內部教育訓練使用，嚴禁外流】               2
 結論一：未來三年矽晶圓受AI帶動，需求成長遠高於供給成長
•   議價權已轉回上游。2026/7美光與環球晶簽5億美元、10年期策略長約；客戶庫存去化進入尾聲，LTA循
    環位置在復甦中段。

•   供給端受五大廠寡占＋擴產紀律約束，年增率長期僅1~3%（僅2017-18、2021擴產潮達6~8%）；需求端
    2023-24連兩年衰退後，2025年+5.8%回升，2026-28年在AI帶動下估連三年+9~12%，供給無彈性遇上需求
    高成長，是本輪缺口的核心結構。

•   價格與供需同步驗證：12吋ASP年均自2025年63美元落底，隨缺口擴大2027/2028年估達101/172美元。

 結論二：預期矽晶圓2027年將供不應求，價格持續向上
•     量的復甦：SEMI統計2025年全球矽晶圓出貨面積12,973 MSI（+5.8%）終結連兩年衰退；2Q26出貨3,573 MSI
      、年增7.4%、季增9.1%，創14季新高；SEMI預估2028年達15,485 MSI改寫歷史新高。需求增速遠高於供給放
      量進程，研究員預估2027下半年正式轉為供不應求，2028年缺口約8%。

•     價格已經落地：2026/7信越、SUMCO、環球晶三大廠同步發出漲價函，12吋常規邏輯晶圓漲5~8%、AI/HPC
      高階晶圓漲18~22%；信越7月法說指各家12吋已滿載、產業進入產能受限狀態，新一輪LTA將反映成本上漲，
      價格上行趨勢確立。

 矽晶圓為寡占、高壁壘的上游材料
 矽晶圓位居半導體最上游，台灣連續16年為最大材料市場
• 矽晶圓是所有晶片製造的起點與地基，約占晶圓製造材料22.9%、居各類材料之首，為需求量最大的半導體材料。台灣是全
 球材料重心：2025年台灣半導體材料市場217億美元、占全球732億美元約29%，連續16年全球之冠（SEMI，2026）；
 SUMCO銷售額34.7%來自台灣。台灣在中游（環球晶全球第三）與下游（台積電代工市占72.3%，1Q26創新高）均居要角，
 上下游完整。

 五道工序中拉晶定生死，資本與技術雙密集
• 產業具三大特性：(1)資本密集——12吋線每10萬片/月產能投資約數十億美元；(2)技術密集——12吋拋光片TTV<0.1μm、表
 面雜質低於百億分之一；(3)強週期＋寡占——景氣循環約3~4年、擴產週期2年以上，五大廠藉多輪併購形成CR5逾90%格局
 ，環球晶即為併購成長典範（2012年Covalent、2016年Topsil與SunEdison，市占由第六升至第三）。

 產品以拋光片與磊晶片為主力，SOI單價達4~5倍

•   矽晶圓依加工深度分為研磨片、拋光片、退火片、磊晶片（外延片）與SOI。拋光片是基準產品，可直接
    投產記憶體與功率元件，也是其他高階產品的襯底；磊晶片附加價值高，信越即以磊晶片為主力；SOI具
    低功耗、抗輻射優勢，單價為一般矽晶圓的4~5倍，其中RF-SOI（5G射頻前端）占約60%。環球晶為少數
    具備全產品線（含SOI、SiC、GaN）的廠商，其美國密蘇里廠即鎖定SOI利基市場。

 結論一：未來三年矽晶圓受AI帶動，需求成長遠高於供給成長
•   議價權已轉回上游。2026/7美光與環球晶簽5億美元、10年期策略長約；客戶庫存去化進入尾聲，LTA循
    環位置在復甦中段。

•   供給端受五大廠寡占＋擴產紀律約束，年增率長期僅1~3%（僅2017-18、2021擴產潮達6~8%）；需求端
    2023-24連兩年衰退後，2025年+5.8%回升，2026-28年在AI帶動下估連三年+9~12%，供給無彈性遇上需求
    高成長，是本輪缺口的核心結構。

AI驅動高速互聯，矽光子落地，CPO續章


    福邦投顧 研究部
      2026/09
 結論
⚫ AI算力需求推升高速光互聯市場。美國四大CSP持續擴大AI資料中心建置，為帶動高速光
  模組需求成長的主要動能。現階段高速光模組出貨仍以800G為主，1.6T預計自2027年逐步
  放量，也帶動矽光(SiPh)模組滲透率提高。

⚫ 矽光模組非新興產品，外型仍沿用既有可插拔光模組規格，但相較傳統光模組，SiPh具備
  元件高度整合及晶圓級量產優勢，隨高速傳輸所需而獲廣泛採用。然而，雷射晶片受限於
  上游InP基板缺貨而供應吃緊。為確保貨源，部分業者已透過長約或預付款方式鎖定供應，
  使掌握貨源者在市場上更具競爭優勢。

⚫ CPO現階段仍面臨光耦合、測試與量產等製程挑戰；對CSP而言，CPO改變其既有可插拔光
  模組的維修與更換模式，加上NPO、XPO等替代架構持續發展，使CPO雖已進入量產階段
  ，短期滲透率仍偏低。展望未來，傳輸頻寬持續提升，為降低傳輸損耗與功率，光引擎將
  逐步靠近交換器ASIC或加速卡，CPO仍具導入需求。此外，NVIDIA持續擴大NVLink
  Fusion生態系，擴大CPO潛在應用市場，惟規模部署時程仍待帶動頻寬需求的新應用興起。

⚫ 相關個股：聯亞(3081)、IET-KY(4971)、寰宇-KY(4991)、聯鈞(3450)、訊芯-KY(6451)、華
  星光(4979)、光聖(6442)、波若威(3163)、上詮(3363)、大立光(3008)

 矽光PIC高度整合光元件並以半導體製程量產
•    矽光模組是指搭載矽光PIC的光模組，矽光PIC透過半導體製程，將調變器、波導等光學功能
     整合於晶片，減少離散元件組裝及光學對準步驟，並有利於晶圓級量產。
•    2016年英特爾即推出矽光子光模組，惟早期高速傳輸需求有限，矽光PIC整合效益尚不顯著；
     隨800G、1.6T以上高速光模組放量，通道數及光元件數量增加，矽光PIC整合優勢浮現。
•    現階段矽光模組仍沿用沿用OSFP、QSFP-DD既有可插拔光模組外型。
•    過去光通訊PIC多採III-V族材料，雷射與光元件可單晶整合，但市場規模較小且製程專用，多
     以IDM方式生產；矽光PIC採CMOS相容製程，可導入成熟矽晶圓代工模式，實現規模量產與
     降低成本，然無法與雷射整合。

•   美網通業者Arista於2026年成立XPO MSA，並展示首代支援200G/lane，頻寬12.8T的可插拔
    XPO模組，後續將發展400G/lane、單模組頻寬25.6T，惟量產與規模商用時程尚未明朗。
    XPO MSA成員橫跨CSP、ASIC、光元件與光模組供應鏈，包括微軟、Marvell、Coherent、
    Lumentum及新易盛等。Arista為Ethernet交換器設備商，主導XPO規格與生態系發展。

•   XPO主打Scale-out應用，強調單一XPO模組可取代8顆OSFP，在有限機箱空間內提高整體傳
    輸頻寬。由於XPO採全新模組機構，交換器須配合重新設計供電、散熱及相關介面，目前規
    格制定與系統平台仍以Arista為主；儘管XPO MSA讓CSP在光模組供應商選擇上更具彈性，
    但在其他交換器業者尚未跟進前，導入XPO亦可能意味對Arista交換器平台的更高依賴。

 Open CPX以標準化介面挑戰NVIDIA封閉式CPO架構
•   美系光傳輸設備商Ciena與Coherent，以及連接器業者Molex、Samtec推動Open CPX MSA，
    透過標準介面讓讓光引擎可拆卸，獨立於ASIC，提高光引擎與ASIC的選擇彈性。

•   Open CPX強調架構選擇彈性，CSP可依系統需求採用NPO或CPO，雷射可選外部雷射或整合
    式雷射方案。

•   Ciena已推出採Open CPX架構的光引擎Vesta，，並以16 顆6.4T光引擎打造總頻寬102.4T的系
    統。Ciena於3Q26法說表示，Vesta樣品已售出，預計2027年開始貢獻營收、2028年放量。

 各種光互聯架構重塑供應鏈價值分配
•   CPO和NPO的供應鏈差異有限，皆由交換器ASIC或加速卡業者主導系統架構，光引擎、雷
    射、FAU、連接器等供應鏈皆配合設計。若CPO滲透率提高，將壓縮傳統可插拔光模組需求
    ，但具雷射組裝能力的業者仍可供應外部雷射
•   CPO的光耦合效率需求提高，使FAU重要性提升。
•   XPO藉提高模組頻寬，延續可插拔方案在高速傳輸的生命週期。
•   Open CPX採用標準介面實現光引擎可拆卸，由於PCB板端需配置CPX連接器，使連接器重
    要性提升。
•   不論採用何種光互連架構，隨AI資料中心傳輸頻寬與光路數持續增加，高密度佈線需求均將
    提升，帶動fiber jumper、fiber harness及fiber shuffle需求，如光聖已切入Google資料中心光纖
    連接供應鏈將明顯受惠。

 CPO長期具導入需求，惟時程仍具不確定性
•   CPO在Scale-out面臨傳統可插拔光模組、XPO與NPO等架構競爭；相較下，台積電認為CPO
    在Scale-up更能發揮高頻寬、低功耗與短距離互連優勢，朝Optical I/O發展。

•   Scale-up 架構目前存在技術路線分歧—Narrow & Fast 與 Wide & Slow；前者持續提高單通道
    速率，以NVIDIA為代表，後者增加道數來擴充頻寬，微軟MOSAIC為較典型方案。

•   展望未來，儘管CPO導入時程受系統架構與成本效益影響，但隨運算規模持續擴大，銅互連
    瓶頸將推動光引擎進一步靠近交換器ASIC或XPU，CPO長期導入趨勢不變。 再者，NVIDIA
    亦透過NVLink Fusion持續擴大Fabric生態系，使採用客製XPU的業者仍可導入NVLink架構

                  Investment thesis
                  Kaori is well positioned to capitalise on rising demand for liquid cooling, and it
                  expects related product shipments to ramp up. The fuel-cell business should be a
                  huge growth driver in 2026-27 to meet AI power infrastructure demand in the US.
                  In the longer term, we believe the company will also benefit from heat-pump
                  demand as Europe is phasing out gas boilers, despite some noise about near-term
                  demand. Kaori has been planning capacity expansion earlier than peers to fully
                  capture demand, with rising exposure to large clients. We thus expect the company
                  to enjoy robust earnings in coming years.

                 Catalysts
                 The major growth catalysts largely depend on fuel-cell projects for AI datacentres
                 taking off, increasing content value in liquid cooling offerings, and a clearer outlook
                 for hydrogen electrolyzer development.

                 Valuation details
                 We adopt a PE-based valuation methodology as we believe the market will mainly
                 focus on the earnings growth outlook, which is better reflected with PE metrics.
                 We base our valuation on 40x PE, which is around +1sd of its five-year average and
                 supported by an 93% EPS Cagr in 2026-28SP, to account for the surging demand
                 for AI server liquid cooling and power infrastructure. We are positive on the
                 company's long-term outlook given its growing stationary fuel cell demand from AI
                 datacentres, as well as its efforts to diversify customer exposure for liquid cooling
                 business. We believe the company can maintain its competitive edge over other
                 cooling players given its expertise in vacuum welding technology to manufacture
                 high-quality products.

                 Investment risks
                 Downside risks: 1) increased competition for Bloom Energy's fuel cell business or
                 new technology solutions replacing fuel cells; 2) slower kick-off of new fuel cell
                 projects for AI datacentres; 3) weaker-than-expected liquid cooling adoption; 4)
                 slower rollout of Europe/US government subsidies for heat pump installations.

       公司簡介：聯茂成立於 1997 年，總部位於新竹縣新埔鎮，主要從事多層印
       刷電路基材及銅箔基板(CCL)的製造、加工與買賣，為台灣主要 CCL 廠之一。
       生產基地主要位於中國江西、無錫及泰國，其中江西廠可生產全部等級，高
       階產品主要於此生產；無錫新廠為未來擴產主力，泰國廠則對應低軌衛星應
       用。產品依介電性能分級，M4 以下為低階產品，往上依序為 M6、M7、M8、
       M9，等級越高，規格與單價越高；目前出貨以 M6 以下為主，1H26 M4 以下
       營收占比約 70%，M7 以上佔比低個位數。主要應用為伺服器 (以 general server
       為主)、網通與低軌衛星。

       E-glass 缺口延續，稼動率回升帶動 2027 年再創新高：目前聯茂主要使用的
       玻纖布 E-glass 報價已達 2.3 美元/平方公尺(見圖表二)，預計將逐月調漲至
       1Q27，主因為：(1)AI server PCB 規格升級帶動用量倍增、 (2)中游電子紗原
       料緊缺，德、日廠產品交期已排至 2029 年、(3)Toyota 自動織布機嚴重緊缺，
       交期達 2 年以上，目前亦排至 2029 年。整體而言，目前造成 CCL 緊缺的主
       因為玻纖布，其中最缺的是用於製作 M6 以下 CCL 的 E-glass；且因 Low-DK
       布單價較 E-glass 高約 3 倍以上，原本生產 E- glass 的廠商多已轉作 Low-DK
       布，在相同投資金額下，新建窯爐與織布機位幾乎全數用於高階 Low-DK 布，
       導致 E-glass 缺口持續擴大。
       聯茂產品線以 M4 以下為主，故 1Q26~3Q26 稼動率在需求強勁下仍受上游
       缺料限制，僅維持在 70~75%，且年底前無新產能開出，今年的大幅成長主
       要來自反映上游原物料漲價。4Q26~1Q27 期間 E-glass 廠中國巨石、泰山玻
       纖新產能開出後，稼動率可望回升至 80%附近，將帶動聯茂營收規模與毛利
       率同步提升，預估 2027 年營收達 930.53 億元(YoY +64.5%)，毛利率達 35.9%。

       General Server 平台換代，PCIe 6 滲透率為規格升級關鍵： General server
       為聯茂規格升級的主軸，2026 年占整體營收逾 50%。兩大客戶 AMD 與 Intel
       近 期 皆 將 進 行 2~3 年 一 次 的 平 台 大 改 版 ， AMD SP7/8(Venice) 與 Intel
       OakStream 均將由 PCIe 5.0 升級至 PCIe 6.0，板材由以 M6 為主轉為以 M7 為
       主，板層數亦由 18~22 層提升至 20~24 層(見圖表四)，此規格升級將使聯茂
       受惠於量價齊揚。以伺服器平台占比而言，AMD 與 Intel 在聯茂營收中的比
       重約為 7:3。參考主要客戶 AMD 新平台的放量時程，SP7(high-end)將 於 4Q26
       推出，SP8(mainstream)將於 1H27 推出，兩者皆支援 PCIe 6.0；預計 AMD 與
       Intel 新平台均將於 4Q26 開始出貨、1Q27 開始放量，將推升 PCIe 6.0 在
       general server 中的滲透率。參考主流研調機構對 general server 出貨量的預
       估，2027 年年增幅約 6~11%，成長幅度遠低於 AI server，因此我們認為帶動
       聯茂規格提升的主要變數為 PCIe 6.0 滲透率，而非出貨量成長。

       聯茂亦將是 Agentic AI、CPU 等題材的主要受惠者之一，預期將為 2027/2028
       年 general server 出貨量帶來進一步上行空間。整體而 言，我們預估 2027 年
       PCIe 6.0 在 general server 平台的滲透率將達 20%，帶動聯茂 M7 營收占比由
       2026 年的 6%提升至 2027 年的 15%，M7 營收金額年增 312%，為 2027 年的
       主要成長動能。

       除了 general server 外，低軌衛星(LEO)也是聯茂 2027 的一大增量，LEO 產

       購，而亞泰金屬於 2027/2028 年均有擴充月產能的計畫，預計聯茂將於 2027
       年 底 有 一 批 上 膠 機 到 貨 ， 產 能 應 可 順 利 開 出 。 其 中 ， 2028 年 新 增 產 能 較
       2026/2027 年多，主因公司未來將供應美系大型 CSP 的 server、switch 用 CCL，
       預計 2H27 可取得驗證結果，故我們預期 2028 年在產能大量開出下仍可維持
       高稼動率，並且公司整體產品報價將有望維持 2027 年的高水準。
       整體而言，我們認為聯茂在 (1)M7 以上占比快速提升、(2)稼動率隨上游瓶頸
       緩解回升至 80%以上、(3)產能規模擴大三項動能下，即使 2027 年後有漲價
       趨緩的風險，獲利仍可維持成長。我們預估 2026/2027/2028 年 EPS 分別為
       23.28/52.49/69.40 元。考量聯茂產品組合較台光電、台燿偏向中低階，短期
       受惠 M6 以下漲價的獲利彈性較大，但長期由產品組合支撐的獲利基礎不如
       同業，故本益比應較同業折價，但短期內聯茂仍是族群中受惠 CCL 漲價幅
       度最大的公司，參考過往兩年的 Forward PE 區間落在 10~26 倍之間，我們
       認為 18 倍的估值為合理評價。

NOMURA

Global Markets Research

Largan Precision  3008.TW 3008 TT

5 October 2026

EQUITY: HANDSETS

Highly sensitive to CPO FAU growth

CPO on track, likely to contribute c.18% of 2028F earnings; but near-term Apple demand could be lighter

Action: Maintain Buy; TP raised to TWD8,300, implying ~23% upside

We reiterate Buy on Largan, and raise our TP to TWD8,300, based on 30x 2028F EPS of TWD276.7 (previously: TWD6,000, on 25x 2028F EPS of TWD240.0). We cut our earnings forecasts by 7.2% and 10.4% for 2026F and 2027F, respectively, to reflect the adverse impact of rising BOM costs on smartphone demand and potential cannibalization of the 18 Pro series by the iPhone Duo. For the first time we incorporate the co-packaged optics fiber array unit (CPO FAU) revenue into our earnings model, by assuming the new business would contribute 1%/18% of 2027/28F earnings. Hence, our 2028F earnings imply 44% y-y growth, driven by CPO FAU and Apple’s (AAPL US, Not rated) camera upgrades. We raise our target P/E from 25x to 30x to reflect Largan’s smooth progress in CPO FAU and a higher sensitivity to its earnings. Every one million units of CPO FAU could contribute c.TWD10 EPS to Largan, in our calculation. The target P/E of 30x exceeds the high end of the stock’s historical trading band (10-25x) since 2015. Largan trades at 35x 2027F P/E.

CPO FA/FAU progress on track

As we highlighted in June and July, Largan can offer a full-range of CPO FAU components and modules, including prism/microlens array (PMLA), FA, and FAU, and has the strength to fully automate the FA and FAU assembly process by leveraging its strong internal machine tool capability. By doing so, Largan’s time-to-market and cost structures for FA and FAU assembly should be competitive vs peers. We estimate the total CPO FAU market could grow from less than 5mn units in 2027F to 30-40mn units in 2028F, and we expect Largan’s market share to be at 10%/15% in 2027/28F (Fig. 1). We assume the ASP to be over USD100, as its major customer will likely prefer Largan to handle FA/FAU assembly rather than just supply components. We believe its fully-automated pilot run line was ready by end-3Q26, and the first MP line could be ready by 1H27F.

Apple: Sunny’s market share loss and continued camera upgrades in 2027-28F

Sunny (2382 HK, Neutral) earlier faced some yield issues with the new variable aperture (VA) main camera lens for the iPhone 18 Pro series, and this could benefit Largan and Genius (3406 TT, Buy). However, given the headwinds of rising memory costs and the potential cannibalization of the 18 Pro series by the iPhone Duo, we see slower iPhone lens shipments from end-2026F to 1H27F, before the 20th anniversary iPhone (Pro Max) and the second-gen iPhone Duo are introduced in 2H27F. We expect a further upgrade in iPhone Pro’s main camera in 2H27F, and introduction of a new periscope camera for the Pro Max in 2H28F.

NOMURA

Global Markets Research

Genius Electronic Optical  3406.TW 3406 TT

5 October 2026

EQUITY: TECHNOLOGY

Fiber connector and CPO an ideal leverage of its capabilities (Erratum)

Quantifying passive fiber connector and CPO opportunities; reiterate Buy

Action: Maintain Buy; raise TP to TWD1,415, implying ~34% upside

We expect AI optical interconnect and communication opportunities (e.g. co-packaged optics fiber array unit [CPO FAU], passive fiber connectors) to transform the traditional optical lens industry over the next 5 years, and believe Taiwanese handset camera lens makers (e.g. Largan [3008 TT, Buy] and Genius) possess inherent advantages to cater to these new markets, given their high-precision molding+plastic injection, optical design, active alignment, optical coating and inspection capabilities, as well as clean-room facilities and sufficient FCF from cash-cow handset lens businesses.

In addition to holding the position of Apple’s (AAPL US, Not rated) No. 2 lens supplier, we believe Genius has obtained ferrule order for passive fiber connectors and will start shipping by end-2026F or early-2027F, as per our channel checks (Genius declines to comment, however). Genius appears well-positioned to supply various CPO FAU components (lens, prism, V groove, FA, etc.) and may potentially handle FAU assembly if requested by customers. We estimate the passive fiber connector and CPO-related new businesses will contribute <3%/16-20% earnings for Genius in 2027F/2028F (details in Fig. 10). Yet, given the high dollar content and long-term growth potential of CPO/FAU related products over the next five years, we believe optical lens makers with inherent advantages in this new field deserve stock re-rating; we thus raise our target P/E to 25x (near the high end of the historical range of 10-30x since 2020), from 17x. We reiterate Buy, and raise our TP to TWD1,415, based on 25x 2028F EPS of TWD56.61 (vs. prior TP of TWD568, based on 17x 2025F EPS of TWD33.4, set two years ago). Genius trades at 25x 2027F P/E.

Apple: Sunny’s market share loss and continued camera upgrades in 2027-28F

Sunny (2382 HK, Neutral) earlier faced some yield issues with the new variable aperture (VA) main camera lens for the iPhone 18 Pro series, and this could benefit Largan (more directly) and Genius (indirectly) in the component landscape. It remains uncertain whether Genius will be introduced as a third lens supplier to iPhone Pro’ main camera in the future, and this poses an upside risk to our forecasts. However, given the headwinds of rising memory costs and the potential cannibalization of the 18 Pro series by the iPhone Duo, we forecast slower iPhone lens shipments from end-2026F to 1H27F, before the 20th anniversary iPhone (Pro Max) and the second-gen iPhone Duo are introduced in 2H27F. We expect further upgrades to the iPhone Pro main camera in 2H27F, and introduction of a new periscope camera for the Pro Max in 2H28F.

(Erratum: This note replaces an earlier published note which incorrectly focused on specific fiber connector. We apologise for any inconvenience this may have caused.)

items.text:
BUY


TSMC (2330.TW)
Earnings preview: Strong growth momentum into 2027; CapEx stepping up
to support long-term demand; reiterate Buy; TP up to NT$3,300

     5 October 2026 | 10:25PM CST | Research | Equity                         PDF     Share    Bookmark     More


TSMC will host its 3Q26 analyst meeting on 15 October. We expect a strong finish to 2026 with a sustained growth
outlook into 2027 for TSMC as demand broadens across AI GPUs/AI ASICs, networking and server CPUs. In
particular, the stronger CPU demand driven by agentic AI represents a key change over the past year. We forecast
2026E/2027E revenue growth of 42.0%/36.9% YoY (USD terms), with GM at 67.2%/67.5%. We also raise our
2027E/2028E CapEx forecasts to US$85bn/US$98bn (vs. US$78bn/US$82bn previously) as we expect TSMC to
further ramp up its capacity investment to support longer-term customer demand.


Strong sequential growth into 4Q26 with modest N2 ramp dilution
We expect TSMC’s 3Q26E revenue to grow 15.3% QoQ, followed by a further 11.0% QoQ increase in 4Q26E
(both in USD terms), supported by continued strength in AI/HPC demand. On profitability, we model GM edging
down to 67.5%/67.3% in 3Q26E/4Q26E, vs. 67.7% in 2Q26, reflecting dilution from the ongoing N2 ramp.


Momentum sustaining into 2027, supported by broader AI demand
We expect TSMC’s revenue to grow 36.9% YoY (vs. 32.0% previously) in USD terms in 2027E, supported by sustained
demand for AI accelerators and networking, alongside an increasingly strong contribution from server CPUs. At our
Communacopia + Technology conference, management highlighted that lower token costs should stimulate greater
AI consumption, while discussions with customers and US CSPs has reinforced confidence in demand and
infrastructure readiness. We believe these trends support continued strength in leading-edge demand, particularly
for both N2 and N3, where management expects supply to remain insufficient despite further expansion.

On the supply side, we expect capacity additions, N5-to-N3 conversion, and productivity gains to support higher
wafer output, while continued CoWoS expansion helps enable associated wafer shipments. We model GM improving
modestly to 67.5% in 2027E (vs. 67.2% in 2026E), supported by higher pricing, favorable product mix, sustained high
utilization and continued productivity gains.


Higher CapEx to support longer-term expansion
We maintain our 2026E CapEx forecast at US$64bn, while raising our 2027E/2028E forecasts to US$85bn/US$98bn
(vs. US$78bn/US$82bn previously), to incorporate 1) cost inflation from equipment vendors, and 2) initial spending
associated with the potential new Texas expansion; however, we expect the new site to only enter mass production
beyond 2032. For capacity, we continue to model our end-2027E/2028E N3/N2 capacity at 200kwpm/140kwpm
and 220kwpm/200kwpm, respectively.


Other key areas in focus for the upcoming analyst meeting
Long-term AI growth outlook: We believe the broadening of AI demand across accelerators, CPUs and networking
further supports TSMC’s long-term growth opportunity. We would look for updated comments from management
 on the key assumptions underpinning its AI outlook through 2030, where demand drivers have strengthened most
over the past year, and the factors that could materially change this outlook.

Longer-term CapEx outlook and US expansion: With customer demand continuing to drive investment in leading-
edge capacity and advanced packaging, we would look for management to provide further direction on its longer-
term CapEx trajectory and the demand visibility supporting these investment decisions. We would also welcome
updated comments on whether customer demand could lead to further expansion in the US beyond current Arizona
site, and the potential timing and scale of such investments.

Foundry competition and technology leadership: We would look for management’s perspective on the evolving
competitive landscape, including Intel, Samsung and Terafab, and the implications for TSMC’s longer-term
positioning. In particular, we would welcome further discussion of its technology leadership, and whether
management expects this gap to widen or narrow across upcoming process generations.

Reiterate Buy; TP raise to NT$3,300 from NT$3,100
We raise our 12m TP to NT$3,300 from NT$3,100 (2330.TW), following our upward earnings revisions. Our TP is
based on a target P/E of 22x (unchanged, benchmarked to 1.0stdv above 5-year avg. forward P/E) applied to our
higher 2027E EPS. Accordingly, we raise our 12 month TP for the ADR to US$660 from US$620, based on an
unchanged FX conversion of USD/TWD of 30.0 and unchanged ADR premium of 20%. Our 22x target P/E multiple is
also benchmarked to TSMC’s trading average of 22x during its previous revenue upcycle where its 3-year revenue
CAGR (2019-2021) was 28%, vs. our 3-year revenue CAGR at 38% during 2025-2028E.
 Our new TP implies 28% (ADR 40%) upside to the last close. As a result, we reiterate our Buy ratings for TSMC/ADR.
We maintain our constructive view on TSMC's long-term growth outlook as we believe the company's solid
technology leadership and execution better positions it vs. peers to capture the industry's long-term structural
growth opportunities, especially in AI.
