Investment Thesis - TSMC (2330.TW/TSM)
TSMC is a leading global foundry company specializing in cutting-edge nodes. Its leading technology stance enables
it to enjoy more than 60% revenue share in the global foundry market. We like TSMC as we believe its solid
technology leadership and execution better position it vs. peers to capture the industry's long-term structural
growth opportunities, particularly in areas such as AI/5G/HPC/EV. In addition, valuation looks attractive in our view,
with the shares trading at the mid-range of their 10-year trading history (P/E: 10-29x). Furthermore, we view TSMC
as the key AI enabler among our Taiwan Semis coverage, thanks to its leadership stance in leading edge nodes and
advanced packaging technology – CoWoS (chip on wafer on substrate). We believe TSMC will achieve its 25% revenue
CAGR target for the next several years, driven primarily by increasing silicon content growth and AI/HPC demand,
with LT GM to remain at 56%+. We are Buy rated.


Price Target Risks and Methodology - TSMC (2330.TW/TSM)
Valuation methodology: We have a 12m TP of NT$3,300, which is derived by applying a target P/E multiple of 22x
to our 2027E EPS. Our 22x target P/E is benchmarked against 1.0stdv above its 5-year trading average. For the ADR
(TSM), we have a 12m TP of US$660, based on a USD/TWD rate of 30.0 and an ADR premium of 20%.
 Key downside risks to our views: (1) further deterioration in end-demand recovery impacting capacity utilization;
(2) slower customer node migrations; (3) slowdown in AI investment resulting in lower long-term semiconductor
content growth; (4) poor yields/execution resulting in worse-than-expected profitability; (5) stronger competition
resulting in ASP/profitability erosion; and (6) unfavorable FX trend or higher-than-expected cost increase weighing
on the margin outlook.

                                              GS Factor Profile
                                              The Goldman Sachs Factor Profile provides investment context for a stock by comparing key attributes to the market (i.e. our universe of rated stocks)
                                              and its sector peers. The four key attributes depicted are: Growth, Financial Returns, Multiple (e.g. valuation) and Integrated (a composite of Growth,
                                              Financial Returns and Multiple). Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple are calculated by using normalized ranks for specific metrics for each stock. The
                                              normalized ranks for the metrics are then averaged and converted into percentiles for the relevant attribute. The precise calculation of each metric may
                                              vary depending on the fiscal year, industry and region, but the standard approach is as follows:
                                              Growth is based on a stock’s forward-looking sales growth, EBITDA growth and EPS growth (for financial stocks, only EPS and sales growth), with a
                                              higher percentile indicating a higher growth company. Financial Returns is based on a stock’s forward-looking ROE, ROCE and CROCI (for financial
                                              stocks, only ROE), with a higher percentile indicating a company with higher financial returns. Multiple is based on a stock’s forward-looking P/E, P/B,
                                              price/dividend (P/D), EV/EBITDA, EV/FCF and EV/Debt Adjusted Cash Flow (DACF) (for financial stocks, only P/E, P/B and P/D), with a higher percentile
                                              indicating a stock trading at a higher multiple. The Integrated percentile is calculated as the average of the Growth percentile, Financial Returns
                                              percentile and (100% - Multiple percentile).

                                              GS Factor Profile
                                              The Goldman Sachs Factor Profile provides investment context for a stock by comparing key attributes to the market (i.e. our universe of rated stocks)
                                              and its sector peers. The four key attributes depicted are: Growth, Financial Returns, Multiple (e.g. valuation) and Integrated (a composite of Growth,
                                              Financial Returns and Multiple). Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple are calculated by using normalized ranks for specific metrics for each stock. The
                                              normalized ranks for the metrics are then averaged and converted into percentiles for the relevant attribute. The precise calculation of each metric may
                                              vary depending on the fiscal year, industry and region, but the standard approach is as follows:
                                              Growth is based on a stock’s forward-looking sales growth, EBITDA growth and EPS growth (for financial stocks, only EPS and sales growth), with a
                                              higher percentile indicating a higher growth company. Financial Returns is based on a stock’s forward-looking ROE, ROCE and CROCI (for financial
                                              stocks, only ROE), with a higher percentile indicating a company with higher financial returns. Multiple is based on a stock’s forward-looking P/E, P/B,
                                              price/dividend (P/D), EV/EBITDA, EV/FCF and EV/Debt Adjusted Cash Flow (DACF) (for financial stocks, only P/E, P/B and P/D), with a higher percentile
                                              indicating a stock trading at a higher multiple. The Integrated percentile is calculated as the average of the Growth percentile, Financial Returns
                                              percentile and (100% - Multiple percentile).

                                                                                                                 productivity gains to support higher wafer output, while continued CoWoS expansion
                                                                                                                 helps enable associated wafer shipments. We model GM improving modestly to 67.5% in
                                                                                                                 2027E (vs. 67.2% in 2026E), supported by higher pricing, favorable product mix,
                                                                                                                 sustained high utilization and continued productivity gains.


                                                                                                                 Higher CapEx to support longer-term expansion
                                                                                                                 We maintain our 2026E CapEx forecast at US$64bn, while raising our 2027E/2028E
                                                                                                                 forecasts to US$85bn/US$98bn (vs. US$78bn/US$82bn previously), to incorporate 1)
                                                                                                                 cost inflation from equipment vendors, and 2) initial spending associated with the
                                                                                                                 potential new Texas expansion; however, we expect the new site to only enter mass
                                                                                                                 production beyond 2032. For capacity, we continue to model our end-2027E/2028E
                                                                                                                 N3/N2 capacity at 200kwpm/140kwpm and 220kwpm/200kwpm, respectively.

                                                               Investment Thesis - TSMC (2330.TW/TSM)
                                                               TSMC is a leading global foundry company specializing in cutting-edge nodes. Its leading
                                                               technology stance enables it to enjoy more than 60% revenue share in the global
                                                               foundry market. We like TSMC as we believe its solid technology leadership and
                                                               execution better position it vs. peers to capture the industry’s long-term structural
                                                               growth opportunities, particularly in areas such as AI/5G/HPC/EV. In addition, valuation
                                                               looks attractive in our view, with the shares trading at the mid-range of their 10-year
                                                               trading history (P/E: 10-29x). Furthermore, we view TSMC as the key AI enabler among
                                                               our Taiwan Semis coverage, thanks to its leadership stance in leading edge nodes and
                                                               advanced packaging technology – CoWoS (chip on wafer on substrate). We believe TSMC
                                                               will achieve its 25% revenue CAGR target for the next several years, driven primarily by
                                                               increasing silicon content growth and AI/HPC demand, with LT GM to remain at 56%+.
                                                               We are Buy rated.

                                              GS Factor Profile
                                              The Goldman Sachs Factor Profile provides investment context for a stock by comparing key attributes to the market (i.e. our universe of rated stocks)
                                              and its sector peers. The four key attributes depicted are: Growth, Financial Returns, Multiple (e.g. valuation) and Integrated (a composite of Growth,
                                              Financial Returns and Multiple). Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple are calculated by using normalized ranks for specific metrics for each stock. The
                                              normalized ranks for the metrics are then averaged and converted into percentiles for the relevant attribute. The precise calculation of each metric may
                                              vary depending on the fiscal year, industry and region, but the standard approach is as follows:
                                              Growth is based on a stock’s forward-looking sales growth, EBITDA growth and EPS growth (for financial stocks, only EPS and sales growth), with a
                                              higher percentile indicating a higher growth company. Financial Returns is based on a stock’s forward-looking ROE, ROCE and CROCI (for financial
                                              stocks, only ROE), with a higher percentile indicating a company with higher financial returns. Multiple is based on a stock’s forward-looking P/E, P/B,
                                              price/dividend (P/D), EV/EBITDA, EV/FCF and EV/Debt Adjusted Cash Flow (DACF) (for financial stocks, only P/E, P/B and P/D), with a higher percentile
                                              indicating a stock trading at a higher multiple. The Integrated percentile is calculated as the average of the Growth percentile, Financial Returns
                                              percentile and (100% - Multiple percentile).

           Global Unichip (3443 TT)
           Share price (5 Oct): TWD8,600.00                    12-mth rating: Buy (1)                                            Information Technology: Taiwan


           Unleashed capacity adding to upside risk

       Rick Hsu                                Summary: Global Unichip (GUC) reported September revenue which closed its 3Q26 top-
       (886) 2 8758 6261                       line 19% above market expectations thanks to its stronger-than-expected turnkey revenue
       rick.hsu@daiwacm-cathay.com.tw
                                               run-rate during the quarter, likely attributable to more capacity support from its key foundry
       Sam Weng                                helping GUC meet strong demand from customers for AI projects. We see upside risk to
       (886) 2 8758 6255                       our/consensus 3Q26 bottom-line estimates but are currently comfortable with our 4Q26
       sam.weng@daiwacm-cathay.com.tw          forecasts despite the 3Q26 revenue beat likely dwarfing QoQ growth for 4Q26. We have a
                                               Buy (1) rating on the counter and will review our model in due course post its quarterly
                                               results release.

                                               Highlight
                                               • 3Q26 top-line beating expectations. GUC released September revenue of TWD7.1bn,
                                                 up 22% MoM (+98% YoY, see chart below), which closed its 3Q26 top-line at
                                                 TWD18.8bn, up 35% QoQ (+118% YoY) for a new record. 3Q26 revenue beat our and
                                                 consensus estimates both by 19% each thanks to its turnkey business (ie, mass-
                                                 production) which contributed TWD16.7bn for 89% of total and beat our estimate by
                                                 22%. We attribute the beat to likely its key foundry continuously unleashing extra
                                                 capacity helping GUC meet the strong customer AI demand during the quarter.

                                               • Quarterly results preview and outlook. We expect GUC to have earned 3Q26 net
                                                 profit of TWD1.7bn, varying not much from the consensus estimate, yet given the top-
                                                 line beat, we now see upside risk to the market expectations. As for 4Q26, our top-line
                                                 and bottom-line forecasts are currently 10% and 26% above the consensus,
                                                 respectively, making us comfortable with our current forecasts since we see the 3Q26
                                                 beat being driven by increased foundry capacity allocation for some shipment pull-in,
                                                 thus dwarfing 4Q26’s QoQ growth on intact AI demand. As flagged in our previous note
                                                 (Upgrading: unleashed capacity adding to growth, 5 August 2026), we continue to
                                                 expect GUC to be a key beneficiary from the strong AI ASIC ramps, including AI CPU
                                                 and accelerators.

                                               Recommendation
                                               We rate GUC Buy (1) with a 12M TP of TWD 5,125 on our 4-quarter forward PER target of
                                               63x. The stock performed well recently which we see as largely pricing in the 3Q26 top-line
                                               beat, therefore only suggesting investors accumulate only on any technical pullback. Key
                                               downside risks are less foundry support and margin execution.

                                                                                            Technology
August ’26 Sell-Through: No signs of recovery
                                                                                                               Nicolas Gaudois
yet                                                                                                                       Analyst
                                                                                                         nicolas.gaudois@ubs.com
                                                                                                                   +65-6495 5148
                                                                                                                    David Vogt
Global smartphone unit sell-through -8.9% YoY August '26 YTD
                                                                                                                         Analyst
Global smartphone unit sell-through (source: Counterpoint) for the month of August                           david.vogt@ubs.com
'26 came in at 85.9m units (-0.1% MoM, -12.3% YoY), marking the ninth consecutive                              +1-212-713 4296
month of YoY sell-through decline (was -12.2%/-10.9% YoY in July/June). By region, all                          Timothy Arcuri
regions except for the US (-3.4% YoY) saw double-digit YoY declines, with India seeing                                    Analyst
the most incremental downside at -17.7% YoY, followed by China (-17.3%), Europe (-                        timothy.arcuri@ubs.com
10.7%) and RoW (-10.1%). Following eight months of significant YoY weakness,                                    +1-415-352 5676
August '26 YTD global smartphone unit sell-through now sits at -8.9% YoY with all                                Randy Abrams
regions well in negative comps (India/China/Europe/RoW/US: -12.3%/-10.5%/-8.7%/-                                        Analyst
8.0%/-4.4% YoY).                                                                                          randy.abrams@ubs.com
                                                                                                              +886-2-8722 7338
Apple outperformance continues, Samsung beginning to rebound                                                       Jimmy Yoon
Apple: YTD iPhone unit sell-through (149.3m units, +8.7% YoY) continues to highlight                                    Analyst
the material outperformance of Apple, which remains the only major OEM (>10% unit                           jimmy.yoon@ubs.com
market share) in positive comps. With key iPhone suppliers optimistic on unit growth in                          +65-6495 4617
'27 (link) on the back of (1) the change in launch schedule (3 models each in 1Q27 and                                 Luke Yoo
3Q27) and (2) the introduction of iPhone Duo (~10m units in first 12 months), we                                         Analyst
continue to forecast Apple strength to continue beyond '26 (UBSe sell-in: +8.5% YoY)                           luke.yoo@ubs.com
and into '27 (+4.7% YoY). Samsung: August '26 sell-through came in at 20.3m units                               +82-2-3702 8132
(+0.9% YoY), returning to positive comps for the first time since March '26, primarily on                             Sunny Lin
the back of the release of the new flagship foldable models (Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra, Fold8,                                Analyst
Flip8) released on August 7th. New foldable sales in August came in at 2.8m units, only                       sunny.lin@ubs.com
0.3m units (or 7.5%) below July+August '25 sales for last year's lineup (Galaxy Z Fold7,                      +886-2-8722 7346
Flip7, Flip7 FE; released on July 25th, 2025) despite two less weeks of sales. Whilst                       Shingo Hirata, CFA
YTD sell-through still remains soft at -4.1% YoY, we believe resilient sales of the new                                   Analyst
flagship model as well as incremental share gains in the mid-range should help Samsung                     shingo.hirata@ubs.com
achieve YoY unit growth (UBSe '26E sell-in: +4.4% YoY). China Android: We continue                              +81-3-5208 6224
to see memory-driven downside materialising with Transsion, Oppo, Vivo, and Xiaomi                                    Jimmy Yu
YoY sell-through decline now at -23.1%/-19.0%/-18.2%/-18.1%.                                                              Analyst
                                                                                                             S1460517080002
Reiterating our sell-in forecasts of -10.0%/-3.0% YoY in '26E/'27E                                            jimmy.yu@ubs.com
                                                                                                              +86-21-3866 8880
We entered the year with a cautious view on the smartphone industry (link) primarily on
the back of rapidly rising memory costs. We also flagged that these dynamics will be                                Joseph Koh
much more penalising for Chinese OEMs focusing on the low-end/mid-range segment.                                         Analyst
                                                                                                             joseph.koh@ubs.com
With the DRAM/NAND upcycles likely to extend until at least 2Q28E/4Q27E and unit                                 +603-2781 1182
sell-through now down 8.9% YoY globally (and on average 16.0% for Transsion, Oppo,
Vivo, and Xiaomi) eight months into the year, we expect to see double-digit YoY unit                                 Kenji Yasui
                                                                                                                          Analyst
decline % and reiterate our '26E sell-in forecast of -10.0% YoY. Heading into '27, with
                                                                                                             kenji.yasui@ubs.com
memory likely to remain an incremental headwind, we expect to see muted demand for                             +81-3-5208 6211
smartphones and see units declining further from a low base. We recently lowered our
YoY unit sell-in forecasts for '27E to -3.0% from +2.0% (link).

Selective on smartphone plays; prefer memory/MLCC suppliers
Within the smartphone supply chain, we continue to prefer MediaTek and Samsung
(both APAC Key Call Buy) as well as ASE, Hon Hai, JCET, Micron, Murata, SEMCO, SK
Hynix and TSMC (all Buy). We remain cautious on LG Display, Maxscend, Xiaomi (all
Neutral) and Largan (Sell). We have Neutral ratings on OEMs Apple and Transsion.

 Valuation Method and Risk Statement
The handset industry, as part of consumer electronics, is cyclically sensitive to the economy
and so upside and downside risks relate to macro drivers. Other downside risks include the
rapid loss of market share due to poor product timing, design or distribution. The supply
chain companies into the handset industry also operate in a highly cyclical market both from
macro concerns and inventory cycles within the supply chain. These companies also operate
in a highly competitive environment with product innovation and R&D investments critical to
success. Valuation methods across the sector include multiple analysis.

                                                                                                                                 2% MoM in February and 2% MoM in March. April, May and June were largely flat, while

                                                                                                                                 with our expectation that TV panel prices would start trending down from 3Q26. That
                                                                                                                                 said, we do not expect a significant decline as supply-side discipline should provide

                                                                                                                                 Below-seasonal Panel Shipments in 2H26

                                                                                                                                 Over the past decade, TV panel shipments have typically been split 49%:51% between 1H
                                                                                                                                 and 2H. In 2026, we expect the mix to skew toward 1H, as TV brands restocked ahead of
                                                                                                                                 major promotional events, including the Winter Olympics in February, the FIFA World Cup
                                                                                                                                 in June-July, and China's 618 shopping festival. We see no clear evidence that these events
                                                                                                                                 will materially boost global TV demand, but they have historically shifted shipment timing
                                                                                                                                 across quarters. As a result, we expect the restocking momentum seen since the start of
                                                                                                                                 the year to fade, with panel order momentum slowing in 2H26.

                                                                                                                                 Display Fab Utilization ~85% in 3Q26

                                                                                                                                 Stronger TV panel shipments supported display fab utilization of ~80% in 4Q24 and 82%
                                                                                                                                 in 1Q25. Utilization declined to 78% in 2Q25 as brands adopted a more cautious stance
                                                                                                                                 following earlier pull-ins and as the impact of China's trade-in program moderated.
                                                                                                                                 Utilization rebounded to 80-85% in 3Q25 as brands restocked for year-end promotions
                                                                                                                                 and remained at similar levels in 4Q25 despite seasonal softness as well as in 1Q26.
                                                                                                                                 Industry utilization stayed broadly flat QoQ, at 80-85% in 2Q26, reflecting continued
                                                                                                                                 supply discipline, followed by a slight uptick in 3Q26.

                                                                                                                                 Over the medium to long term, we continue to believe the display industry is undergoing
                                                                                                                                 structural change. Chinese panel makers have shifted their focus from top-line growth to
                                                                                                                                 profitability, while lower government subsidies have reinforced supply discipline. We
                                                                                                                                 believe investors increasingly recognize that the industry's production-to-order model can
                                                                                                                                 remain sustainable, particularly as panel price cycles shortened to quarters in 2023-24 vs.
                                                                                                                                 multiyear cycles in the previous decade. Consolidation actions, including LG Display's sale
                                                                                                                                 of its Gen 8.5 Guangzhou fab to TCL and Sharp's closure of its Gen 10 Sakai fab, also

                          Risk/Reward Largely Fair

                          We view risk-reward as broadly balanced following the recent correction in panel stocks.
                          Below are our current views:

                              • AUO (2409.TW, Derrick Yang): We rate AUO Equal-weight with a PT of NT
                                 $27.00, based on a 1.4x 2026e P/B multiple. While we believe the current round of
                                 TV panel price increases is nearing an end, major panel makers should continue to
                                 demonstrate solid supply discipline, providing downside support. We appreciate
                                 AUO's efforts to diversify its business, but meaningful earnings contributions are
                                 likely to take time.
                              • BOE (000725.SZ, Derrick Yang): We prefer BOE due to its scale advantage,
                                 higher exposure to display and faster progress in glass core substrates. Our PT of
                                 Rmb9.30 is based on 2.5x 2026e P/B, which we view as reasonable given our
                                 estimated ROE of 5-8% over 2026-28 compared with BOE's average P/B of 1.1x and
                                 ROE of 2-4% during 2023-25.
                              • Innolux (3481.TW, Derrick Yang): In semiconductors, our supply-chain checks
                                 suggest that Innolux is participating in a foundry customer's glass core substrate
                                 project. However, we do not expect meaningful contributions before 2028, and
                                 additional competitors could enter as the industry moves toward mass production.
                                 We maintain our Equal-weight rating and PT of NT$60.00, based on a 2.1x 2026e
                                 P/B multiple.
                              • LG Display (034220.KS, Ryan Kim): Meaningful OLED revenue contribution
                                 should increasingly improve earnings from 2H25, but potentially weaker end-
                                 markets keep us from turning bullish on LGD. The stock trades at 0.6x 2026e P/B
                                 vs. a historical mid-cycle level of 0.5x.
                              • TCL (000100.SZ, Derrick Yang): We are EW with a price target of Rmb4.70 (1.7x
                                 2026e P/B). The stock is trading at 1.7x 2026e P/B vs. its mid-cycle average of 1.4x
                                 since 2022.


                              • Greater China DDIC supply chain implications – Novatek (3034.TW, Daniel Yen):
                                 Our Underweight thesis reflects weaker PC, smartphone and automotive demand,
                                 gross margin pressure, and a lack of new growth drivers. That said, Novatek's
                                 OLED DDI roadmap appears more competitive than those of its key Korean peers
                                 in terms of both performance and cost, helping it gain share in Apple's iPhone
                                 supply chain.

                          Where We Could Be Wrong

                            • Stronger end demand: If end demand for major applications turns out to be better
                              than expected, there could be stronger panel shipments and less panel price
                              pressure.
                            • More stringent output control: If major panel makers collectively adjust
                              utilization to an extreme extent, they could mitigate pricing pressure in the case of
                              softer demand.
                            • Non-commodity display business: If the non-commodity business progresses
                              faster than expected, panel makers could show better financial results.

UMC is well positioned for Silicon Photonic IC (PIC) foundry
                     In our previous Foundry Floorplan, we presented a constructive view on UMC given its AI-
                     related revenue. Management indicated AI revenue of US$300mn this year (3-5% of
                     revenue), potentially more than tripling to US$1bn in three years (2029).

                     UMC has a capacity expansion plan to capture AI demand, including a clean room for
                     advanced packaging for AI chips, such as wafer-on-wafer and memory-on-memory stacking.

                     Some investors remain on the sidelines amid ongoing smartphone and PC demand
                     weakness, and we have seen some order cuts of PC semis recently. Some think a UMC
                     price hike in 2027 wouldn’t go through, but we see two growth drivers helping it
                     successfully hike wafer price for 8-inch in 2027: 1) Samsung DDI outsourcing, and 2)
                     growing SiPh PIC demand, in particular after UMC introduced its 400Gb per lane solution
                     (PIC + TFLN) solution.

                     How UMC is differentiated in PIC foundry

                     According to UMC, InP and TFLN are the two most promising solutions, as they are much
                     more mature than the other contenders. InP is facing severe shortage, adding to TFLN’s
                     momentum.

                     UMC Group’s TFLN program started in 2021 with 6” in mass production and 8” in
                     sampling. TFLN's strengths include low loss, high bandwidth (> 110 GHz), good thermal
                     stability, and strong linearity.

                     Integrating TFLN with PIC is a challenge as well as an opportunity. Advanced packaging
                     schemes and micro transfer printing are both seen as promising candidates. UMC is
                     developing the integration technology, leveraging its expertise in PIC, TFLN, and advanced
                     packaging.

                     Adoption of higher-performance modulators (TFLN/InP) and improvement in photo diodes
                     are key factors affecting deployment of plain-vanilla (non-WDM, IM/DD) DCIs with 400
                     Gbps/channel performance and beyond, which is very close to TSMC's mainstream PIC
                     technology Micro Ring.

技術創新再創新、營收翻倍再翻倍
● 2Q26 財報 EPS 優於預期、2H26 逐季顯著季增趨勢明確
● 設備產能持續翻倍，搭配 ASP 同步成長捉注獲利增
● TGV-ICP 預估 2H28 起加速放量，並為中長期營運支柱

2Q26 毛利率小幅遜於預期：創新服務 2Q26 營收 3.6 億元；毛利率 79.1% 受制日本原料商交期變長導致整體出貨遞延，故小幅遜於預期；惟在營收規模效益加持下整體毛利率仍維持 84.5%，EPS 3.4 元，均小幅優於前手預期。

2H26 探針卡封裝設備出貨加速，預期營運逐季顯著成長：鑑於公司 2Q26 存貨中原料、在製品均已顯著回升，我們認為後續出貨速度將有所改善，預期每月平均出貨 8-9 台，掩注 2H26 營運顯著季增；且因業務貢獻以雙臂式 MEMS 植針機為主，故亦看好 2H26 毛利率維持 80%+。

探針卡客戶擴產腳步積極，對應公司 2026-2028 年逐年翻倍擴產展望：我們預期國際探針卡客戶規劃 2027 年將擴產至 2,000 萬針，為當前產能近 3 倍規模；公司作為專屬植針機設備供應商，目前亦加速於台中二／三廠備戰產能，我們更預期在此客戶強勁展望下，公司 2026/2027/2028 年雙臂植針機擴產展望分別達 75/150/300 台，且因設備代數持續升級刺激 ASP 成長、及部分配備 AOI 檢測的非 MEMS 植針機台單價亦相對優患，故預估 2026/2027/2028 年設備營收佔比仍達 90%/85%/75%。

2027 年預期植針代工為主，材料包/銅柱模組 2H27 接續貢獻：參考客戶導入現況，我們預期 2026/2027 年除設備外主要貢獻皆來自植針代工，且因其毛利率更勝材料包，有利毛利率攀升。不同於 2H27 起隨客戶需求加持，預估材料包及銅柱模組將接棒貢獻；此外，我們發現公司銅柱模組技術在 CPO 應用具採用價值，為未來值得追蹤之處。

持續提前準備 TGV-ICP 產能，預估 2H28 逐步放量：我們現依大廠晶片藍圖進程，調整 TGV-ICP 放量時間點至 2H28，但因客戶需求龐大可期，故預期 2029-2030 年公司相關產能仍有望快速滿載，並成為 2028 年後營運成長主力，而公司也須於 2027 年起更偕促產能因應客戶所需。

產業趨勢明確且成長爆發力具延續性，給予「買進」評等：我們預估 2026/2027/2028 年 EPS 將為 16.7、46.4、110.3 元，考量在產業趨勢明確下公司展望爆發力同具延續性，對高評價亦具支持，故給予「買進」建議，目標價為 2,730 元（2H27-1H28 EPS*40 倍 PER）。

風險因子：產能擴充速度不如預期、TGV-ICP 量產時程延後。

技嘉 2376 TT（電子–電腦及週邊設備）

AI 爆發帶動 26~27 年獲利創高

強力買進－維持強力買進

目標價：535 元　+43.2%
收盤價：373.50 元

投資與評價

1. 3Q26 在客戶資料中心完成積極拉貨下，估營收創新高，技鋼占比逾八成，產品結構優化使毛利率明顯跳升，獲利同創新高，EPS 11.9 元。
2. 隨 Nebius 拉貨強勁，技嘉能見度已看到 1H27，今年產能將翻倍成長，估營收、獲利將逐季創高，2H26 獲利 YoY+172%、EPS 23 元。
3. 預期技鋼 27 年佔比拉升至 85%，貢獻技嘉今年、明年獲利再創新高，EPS 分別達 42.2 元、51.7 元，維持強力買進評等，上修目標價至 535 元。
（以稀釋後 26 年獲利估 13.5x 評價）

重點更新

3Q26 營收、獲利將再創高

估技嘉 3Q26 營收 1,587 億元，QoQ+10%、YoY+100%，主要因客戶資料中心完成積極拉貨硬體，日本季高階顯卡銷售強勁。估技鋼占比逾八成，其中 GB 比重約 20~25%，在產品組合優化且部分低價庫存貢獻，加上消費產品銷售回穩，估毛利率將回升至 11.4%，營業利益 YoY+245%至 118.6 億元，上修稅後獲利 20%至 EPS 11.9 元，獲利將再創歷史新高。

技鋼在手訂單能見度已看到 1H27

AI 在手訂單已達 1H27，較過往一季明顯提升，主因 Nebius 硬體集中於 2H26 進駐，客戶大型合約須確保供應鏈產能，加上主權 AI 貢獻，預期 2H26 技嘉營收獲利皆翻倍成長，且營收增幅延續到 1H27，上修 4Q26 營收至 1,742 億元，YoY+95%。Vera Rubin 將有完整貢獻，機櫃比重估三成以上。此外，高端顯卡通路售價還高於 MSRP，預期消費產品營收季增，毛利率小幅回落下，EPS 12.5 元，獲利再創新高。2H26 上修獲利 21%至 163.7 億元，YoY+172%、EPS 23 元（已考量 ECB 對股本膨脹 5.97%影響）

技嘉隨客戶 Nebius 2H26~1H27 DC 建置完成而營運增速

Nebius 10 月全面調漲租賃價格，其中，Nvidia Blackwell 上調 19~21%，Hooper 上調 17~20%，隨 1H27 客戶數個新資料中心落成，且繼續交付 Hyperscaler 訂單，最大供應商技嘉今年產能翻倍成長，受惠訂單強勁且確認度提升，上修技嘉 2026 年、2027 年營收至 YoY+73%、37%，技鋼分別年增 120%、46%，27 年佔比拉升至 85%，更多垂直整合及 GADU 加入下，獲利持續創高，上修今、明年獲利 12%、16%至 EPS 42.16 元、51.73 元。

MEMO


            Nan Ya Printed Circuit Board Corp (8046 TT)
            Share price (2 Oct): TWD1,460.00                    12-mth rating: Buy (1)                                            Information Technology: Taiwan


            August results released: improving profitability continuously

       Sheng Cheng                              Summary: NYPCB released its August results (for pre-tax profit and net profit) after
       (886) 2 8758 6253                        market hours on 2 October mainly due to recent volatile share price movements. Net profit
       sheng.cheng@daiwacm-cathay.com.tw
                                                in August 2026 came in at TWD1,092m (EPS: TWD1.69), up 665% YoY, with pre-tax profit
       Thomas Kim                               at TWD1,486m (pre-tax margin at 27.8%). The August pre-tax margin of 27.8% is close to
       (886) 2 8758 6249                        our current forecast (28.5%/32.9% in 3Q26E/4Q26E). As we expect limited impact from
       thomas.kim@daiwacm-cathay.com.tw         non-ops and on opex in August, we infer the gross margin in August should have reached
                                                to c.30-31% (vs. our forecast c.30.3/34.4% in 3Q26E/4Q26E). This echoes our previous
                                                notes (Spec upgrade to drive additional ABF substrate demand); we expect NYPCB’s
                                                gross margin will recover to c.30% after Kunshan’s yield rate improvement in August. As
                                                such, we believe the August results to be largely on track with market expectations.
                                                However, we believe the share price upside will come from BT substrate, where we should
                                                see better progress in its implementing price hikes now (vs. limited visibility earlier in
                                                September). We expect NYPCB to raise ASP of BT substrates by single digits QoQ in
                                                4Q26 and +20% QoQ in 1Q27. This is aligned with our previous comment (Clarification on
                                                “no intention to hike price from 4Q26”) that we expect BT substrate prices will accelerate
                                                again in 2027 despite a lower-than-expected price hike in 4Q26E. We view NYPCB’s
                                                August results announcement as a near-term price catalyst. We have a Buy rating (1) on
                                                NYPCB with a 12-month TP of TWD2,460. Downside risk: weaker-than-expected demand
                                                for switches/PCs/ smartphones.

                                 We are positive on the PCB/CCL sector into 2027/28, with a strong upgrade cycle, and the

                                         Implications for PCB/CCL
                                         We think the TPU supply chain will enjoy the biggest growth in 2027/28 along with strong unit
                                         growth and content value upgrades among all the GPU/ASICs. Shipments are expected to
                                         reach 8.5m/12m in 2027/28 vs 3.6m in 2026. We view increasing compute power, higher HBM
                                         density, and a doubling of ICI bandwidth as pushing PCB designs toward significantly higher
                                         routing density, tighter L/S, more advanced CCL, smaller via structures, and multi-stage
                                         lamination to maintain signal integrity and shorten electrical paths.

                                         We observed that TPU’s PCB ASP has risen 2.5x from TPU V5 to V8, and 4x for the 400Gbps
                                         switch to 800Gbps. In addition, we estimate 2.6x growth in TPU unit demand from 2025E-27E
                                         and 3x expansion in the 400bps/800Gbps AI switch market by 2028 versus 2025, or 30%
                                         growth in total, making TAM growth exponential in these years.

                                         The table below illustrates the structure of Google TPU v8. One rack will contain eight
                                         compute trays, with each tray equipped with four TPUs, four NICs, four optical modules as
                                         well as two CPUs (Axiom). TOR (Top-Of-Rack)/OCS will connect those racks together to form
                                         a superpod (via the Virgo network) and the Juniper network to connect with other functions.
                                         The increasing compute power and connectivity represents significant content value growth
                                         for PCB/CCL based on those performance upgrades and data transmission.

                                         To support the performance upgrades, TPU PCB architecture is shifting from standard
                                         multilayer (Ghostfish) to N+M structures using dual-grade CCL and multi-lamination in
                                         Zebrafish and Sunfish, and ultimately to HDI PCB in Humufish. These transitions lift PCB ASPs
                                         by 30% in Ghostfish, 80%–90% in Sunfish/Zebrafish. Based on our estimates, content value
                                         per rack for PCB is up to USD30k-40k and CCL USD12-18k for TPU v8 (vs USD20k/7k in
                                         v7). We expect another 40%–50% in Humufish with HDI adoption. Into TPU V10, given
                                         that TDP will further double to 10kW, we can assume PCB/CCL will be further upgraded
                                         to meet the higher requirement.

                                 witnessed several rounds of price hikes already this year and expect more. Besides, our
                                 channel check suggests that CSPs are working closely with PCB/CCL makers for LTAs to
                                 secure advanced capacity and smooth the production process. This section will discuss these
                                 two issues and implications for the supply chain.

                                 Price hikes will likely continue
                                 Our supply chain checks suggest that CCL makers are increasing prices by 50%-100% YTD to
                                 reflect 1) organic material upgrades under the supply constraint, 2) a shortage inf upstream
                                 materials supply and price hikes (resin, copper foil and glass cloth), and 3) longer and more
                                 complex laminate process for more advanced CCL. We see price hikes across the board from
                                 all production lines from M8 material to M4 because tier 1 makers are allocating more
                                 capacity for advanced materials (which requires a longer processing time resulting in lower
                                 production volume). As such, entry-level products will be excluded and will partially shift to
                                 second-tier vendors.

                                 Based on current visibility, we expect more waves of price hikes in CCL in 2H26 and 1H27. We
                                 think each round will be 10%-15%. We assume better profitability for CCL makers in future
                                 quarters owing to 1) higher UTR under a supply constraint, 2) continued price hikes and 3)
                                 favorable product mix along with product migration.

                                 Are LTAs becoming new norm for PCB/CCL?
                                 Given the tight supply conditions and strong PCB/CCL demand for the foreseeable future, we
                                 are also hearing that CSPs are aggressively approaching PCB and CCL makers for LTAs to
                                 secure capacity. Terms will vary from vendor to vendor. However, those discussions send a
                                 clear message that end users are securing high-end PCB/CCL capacity by prepayment and
                                 LTAs for the next few years, because the overall industry may continue to remain
                                 undersupplied. Also, we reckon prepayment 1) will ease supply chain pressure on capex/cash
                                 flow, 2) make the supply chain more willing to invest under longer order visibility and secured
                                 shipment volume, and 3) improve supply chain management with better profitability. Below

                                         implications
                                         Given the fast development of PCB design, there is lots of noise in the supply chain about the
                                         future PCB demand outlook. This section will discuss the latest developments in the PCB

                                         mSAP is becoming a standard for optical beyond 1.6T
                                         mSAP (Modified Semi-Additive Process) is not a new technology. It is an advanced PCB
                                         manufacturing method that builds fine circuit traces by electroplating copper onto a thin
                                         layer rather than etching away thick copper. It allows PCB to further shrink its L/S to below
                                         30um (compared to 30-50um for traditional etching). As such, PCB can support higher
                                         density to support advanced electronic devices with a smaller/complex form factor.

                                 M9 materials based on PPO/HC resin are no longer sufficient to meet Nvidia’s performance
                                 requirements. PTFE has better/stable signal performance (low Dk/Df) and the current hybrid
                                 solution with no glass cloth can reduce the usage of Q-glass, which is under a supply
                                 constraint. However, the hybrid solution is difficult to process (laminate/drill), making its
                                 yield rate very low and higher manufacturing costs. Also, the new material will take longer
                                 time for qualification.

                                 Implication to supply chain: We don’t think PTFE will become mainstream material in AI
                                 servers in the near future considering its low yield rate and high cost. It is more likely to be
                                 adopted in areas which require extremely low Dk/Df like Nvidia is testing it for switch boards
                                 and potentially backplane.

                                 For PTFE CCL supply, we think Shengyi will be the first source given its track record with
                                 Nvidia. EMC/Taiflex camp will likely be the second source potentially (EMC supplies M9 PP
                                 and Taiflex supplies PTFE CCL). For PCB supply, we think the major suppliers will be Chinese-
                                 based PCB vendors (SCC, Kinwong, WUS and VGT for example) and the yield rate is still low
                                 (below 30%).

                                 CPO may trigger CCL de-spec?
                                 CPO is an advanced heterogeneous integration of optics and silicon devices in a single form.
                                 It enables the integration of both PIC and EIC and packages them in a modular form factor
                                 along with switches or XPU (including ASIC) via substrate or interposer to support high-speed
                                 transmission and power saving. In traditional systems, electronic signals are converted to
                                 optical signals with signal loss and higher power consumption. CPO, however, places the
                                 optical engines closer to the switch ASIC or xPU, reducing the distance that signals need to
                                 travel and improving the overall performance.

                                 Most common data transmission involves using a transceiver module to input data into the
                                 switch ASIC for computing, which must pass through the PCB. For switches, the PCB distance
                                 between the transceiver module and the switch ASIC is approximately 11 to 12 inches or
                                 ±300mm. This results in signal loss and reduces the switch ASIC’s signal integrity from 40 dBm
                                 to 20 dBm, implying a 50% signal loss. This is despite industry efforts to develop advanced
                                 low Df/Dk CCL to reduce signal loss and latency. As such, placing the optical engine next to
                                 the switch IC will efficiently resolve this problem as illustrated in figure below.

                                 Implication for the supply chain: The CPO’s purpose is to minimize the data transmission
                                 on the PCB, allowing high-speed data transmission to take place within the IC level. In this
                                 case, PCB in switch systems may no longer require the low-Df/Dk CCL material compared to
                                 its use of high-end low Df/Dk CCL (M6-M8) for 400Gbps and 800Gbps switch today. As such,
                                 some people may be concerned that the adoption of CPO will slow down the further
                                 migration of CCL.

                                 More impact on CCL side but manageable
                                 As discussed above, we believe the adoption of CPO will impact the CCL side more (material
                                 change) instead of the PCB side. However, we don’t think it will become an immediate threat
                                 and the overall impact should be manageable, because 1) The design of CPO is not finalized
                                 and still faces challenges in higher manufacutring costs, lower yield rate, and reliability issues,
                                 2) Nvidia is more aggressive in CPO solutions while other vendors (like Google) still stick with
                                 existing solutions, and 3) the overall CCL industry is undersupplied and material upgrades of
                                 more and more new applications are taking place in to fulfill future demand.

                                 Hence, our conclusion is 1) CPO penetration takes time and the initial impact will be more in
                                 the Nvidia supply chain instead of the entire AI supply chain for CCL makers, and 2) the overall
                                 trend for CCL material upgrades will remain strong as other non-CPO application demand
                                 remains strong and the overall industry is still undersupplied.

                                           We see an increasing trend for adopting HDI in advanced AI acclerators: 1) it shortens high-
                                           frequency signal paths, reducing signal attenuation and latency, 2) it increases circuit density
                                           through microvia technology, including blind and buried vias, 3) it saves internal space and
                                           4) it optimizes heat dissipation efficiency. HDI normally requires fewer layers compared to
                                           conventional multi-lam PCB due to its higher density, but HDI PCB is still more challenging
                                           because it requires multiple cycles of laser drilling, sequential buildup, and ultra-fine feature
                                           formation. The longer processing and lower yield rate will further drive up content value for
                                           PCB.

Goldilocks

We resume coverage of the PCB/CCL industry, focusing primarily on Google’s TPU supply chain, which we believe will deliver the strongest and most sustainable growth through 2028 and beyond. We forecast aggregate TPU volumes to more than triple between 2025/26 and 2028, far outpacing competing platforms. Critically, we project a surge in the content value of next-generation TPU ASICs. As Google integrates more advanced logic and HBM chiplets into a single compute module, we project TPU content value to increase five- to tenfold over the next three to four years. Accordingly, we estimate that the addressable PCB content value alone could quadruple from 2026 to 2029. Equally vital is Google’s longstanding leadership in optical connectivity for its Superpods. The upcoming doubling of switch speeds and interconnect bandwidth will act as a secondary tailwind, further lifting PCB content value. Consequently, we expect the PCB/CCL market to experience continuous pricing power and a possibility of LTAs forming, mirroring the supply dynamics seen in the memory industry. Within the key TPU vendor matrix, we resume coverage of ISU Petasys and EMC with BUY ratings and target prices of KRW 270k and TWD 10,000, respectively. We also initiate coverage of TTM with a BUY rating and a target price of $236. Risks include end demand, execution, and US option on AI data centre expansion.

Why Google’s TPUs?

We forecast TPU’s volume to more than triple to 12m units in 2028 (8.5mn in 2027) from 3.6mn in 2026, encompassing both in-house deployment and allocations to third-party AI labs via ASIC services. The strong volume is evident by its massive $520bn cloud service backlog orders in C2Q26. At the same time, TPU is expected to quadruple in TPU V9 (mid-28) vs V8 (2H26) and could double again in V10 (2029) as Google squeezes more chiplets into its ASIC designs. The complexity of design for PCB (upgrade to 50L+ or HDI) and CCL (upgrade to M8/M9 material or even PTFE) represents at least 50%-100% expansion in ASP in each generation. Furthermore, networking is expected to see a similar upgrade trend in PCB/CCL, as scale-up architectures and bandwidth requirement rise, especially from 400Gbps to 800G/1.6Tbps.

LTA likely becomes new norm under strong demand and supply constraint

Our supply chain survey indicated increasing discussion about long-term agreements (LTA) over the PCB and CCL supply chain with CSPs. Terms may be different from vendor to vendor, and most of them are still under discussion at this stage. However, those discussions send a clear message that end users are securing high-end PCB/CCL capacity by prepayment and LTAs for the next few years, because the overall industry may continue to remain undersupplied. Also, we reckon prepayment 1) will ease supply chain pressure on capex/cash flow, 2) make the supply chain more willing to invest given longer visibility and secured shipment, and 3) improve supply chain management with better profitability. We believe this will further boost P/E for the supply chain, if LTAs are confirmed, with longer visibility and stable order backlogs.

We prefer TPU supply chain into 2027/28: buy on EMC, ISU and TTM

The TPU supply chain will be the biggest winner into 2027/28 with strong unit growth and content value upgrades. Shipments are expected to reach 8.5/12m in 2027/28 vs 3.6m in 2026. Content value per rack for PCBs is up to USD30k-40k and CCL USD12k-18k for TPU v8 (vs USD20k/7k in v7). We expect another 40%-50% in v9 with HDI adoption. We like EMC for its leading position and expect TPU/800Gbps switches to become the company’s key earnings driver. We set our TP at NT$10,000, with 30x FY27/28 PER. ISU is uniquely positioned to capture these secular trends due to its high exposure to Google and networking. We have a BUY and a TP of KRW270,000 on 30x FY27/28 PER. Lastly, TTM is the best proxy in the United States to capture both AI server and national defence trends with better profitability and irreplaceability

Starlink V3 satellites deliver ~10x increase in downlink capacity
SpaceX successfully launched Starship Flight 14 on September 28, 2026 (see John
Hodulik's note for more detail), deploying 26 Starlink V3 satellites into the orbit and
marking the beginning of Starlink's next generation upgrade cycle. The V3 platform
represents a major architecture upgrade over the existing V2 and V2 Mini satellites,
delivering significantly higher throughput, greater beamforming capability, and
expanded backhaul capacity. Rather than expanding coverage, the V3 rollout is aimed at
addressing Starlink's increasingly important network-capacity constraint. While V2
established global broadband coverage, V3 is designed to support much larger traffic
loads across consumer broadband, enterprise connectivity, mobility applications, and
future AI-driven workload, while lowering the cost per bit delivered. Importantly, the
technology developed for the V3 satellite is also expected to support the migration of
Starlink Mobile from V1 to V2, enabling near terrestrial-like LTE connectivity directly to
standard, unmodified cellular devices.

As Starlink's subscriber base continues to expand, capacity constraints have become
increasingly visible in densely populated regions, resulting in slower speed and traffic
management measures for heavy users. With global coverage largely established, the
key challenge is no longer the number of satellites in orbit, but the amount of
throughput each satellite can deliver. At the same time, growing congestion at Starlink's
current operating altitude of approximately 550 km has increased pressure on the orbital
resource. To address both issues, Starlink's new-generation V3 satellites are designed to
operate at a lower altitude of roughly 350 km, which should reduce end-user latency
from around 40-50 ms to below 20 ms, while also improving overall networking
responsiveness.

Figure 1: Starlink V3 vs V2 satellite key specification comparisons

                                         Starlink V3                Starlink V2
Orbit                                      350 km                     550 km
Downlink Capacity                     1,000 Gbps (1 Tbps)            96 Gbps
Uplink Capacity                           160 Gbps                   7-8 Gbps
Downlink Beams                              2,048                       192
Uplink Beams                                2,048                       144
RF Backhaul Capacity                       1.2 Tbps                  140 Gbps
Bands                          Ka, Ku, V, E, W, D (potential)       Ka, Ku, V, E
Laser Links                              6 x 400 Gbps              3 x 200 Gbps

Solar Power                                   2x                      Baseline
Satellite Mass                            ~2,000 kg                  ~800 kg
Launch Vehicle                             Starship                   Falcon 9

Source: Company data, UBS estimates


The V3 platform represents a step-function increase in network capacity over the current
V2 Mini generation. According to SpaceX, each V3 satellite is capable of delivering up to
1 Tbps of downlink throughput and 160 Gbps of uplink throughput, representing
approximately a 10x increase in downlink capacity versus V2 (~96 Gbps) and a 22x
increase in uplink capacity (~7 Gbps). V3 further expands the number of independently
steerable communication beams to 2,048 for both downlink and uplink, compared with
192 downlink beams and 144 uplink beams on V2 satellites. These improvements are
enabled by a new generation of in-house designed beamforming chips, more powerful
modem processors, and a much denser phased-array antenna architecture.

Beyond improving access capacity, V3 also introduces meaningful upgrades to Starlink's
network backbone. While retaining Ku- and Ka-band for user connectivity, V3 expands
backhaul capacity through broader utilization of E-band and V-band spectrum, while
adding support for W-band frequencies. Each satellite also carries four quad-band RF
backhaul antennas and six 400-Gbps optical inter-satellite laser links, materially
increasing overall network transport capacity. These enhancements are particularly
important as Starlink scales enterprise networking, aviation, and maritime connectivity,
all of which place significantly greater demands on uplink and backhaul resources than

 traditional residential broadband. This also supports the migration of Starlink Mobile
satellite upgrade to V2, which enables 4x the number of beams compared to the V1 and
4x the channel bandwidth, supporting the full range of mobile broadband data and
voice service.

The substantial performance gains offered by V3 come with a corresponding increase in
satellite size, power consumption, and system complexity. Supporting 10× higher
throughput requires larger phased array antennas, more advanced beamforming
hardware, higher-performance onboard processing, and solar arrays generating roughly
twice the power of current V2 satellites. In addition, operating at approximately 350 km
exposes V3 satellites to materially higher atmospheric drag compared with the 550 km
orbit used by V2. To maintain orbit, conduct regular station-keeping maneuvers, and
enable controlled end-of-life de-orbiting, V3 requires larger propulsion systems and
greater propellant capacity. As a result, V3 satellite mass is expected to exceed 2,000 kg,
compared with ~800 kg for V2 Mini. The larger form factor effectively necessitates a
transition from SpaceX's Falcon 9 launch vehicle to Starship, whose payload capacity is
specifically intended to support deployment of the V3 constellation.

We provide a deep dive analysis based on our industry checks, recent management
discussions, and Starlink deployment assumptions from our US telecom team. The
transition from Starlink V2 to V3 represents one of the most significant radio frequency
(RF) content upgrades across the satellite communication supply chain. While SpaceX
has not publicly disclosed the exact number of power amplifiers (PAs) or low noise
amplifiers (LNAs) integrated into each satellite, the published system specifications point
to a substantial increase in RF front-end content. Key drivers: 1) a ~10x increase in
downlink capacity, 2) a ~22x increase in uplink capacity, 3) a 10-14x increase in beam
counts, 4) the addition of E/V/W-band backhaul payload, and 5) full-scale deployment of
D2C functionality for Mobile V2.

We assume each radiating antenna element corresponds to a dedicated RF channel,
requiring one PA for transmission and 1-2 LNAs for receiving. Based on our industry
checks, we believe both V3 and V2 Mini feature five Ku-band antenna panels, where we
assume the V3 satellite includes a 32 x 64 high-density matrix, resulting in a total of
2,048 radiating elements per panel. For V2, we estimate 512 elements per panel, based
on 16 x 32 configuration. Under these assumptions, total Ku-band PA and LNA content
increases to ~20,480 units per V3 satellite, versus ~5,120 units for V2 Mini.

A similar content expansion is likely occurring within the gateway backhaul system. We
believe V3 employs four gateway panels vs three for V2 Mini, and has upgraded the
gateway panels from a 16 x 16 architecture in V2 to a denser 32 x 32 configuration,
increasing element count from 256 to 1,024 per panel. The higher element density is
necessary to support the higher frequency requirements associated with E-, V-band, and
ultra-high frequency W-band (up to 110 GHz). As a result, we estimate total gateway PA
and LNA content rises to ~12,288 units per V3 satellite, up from 2,304 units for V2 Mini.

D2C capability provides a further layer of RF content growth. After D2C functions were
initially tested on Starlink Mobile V1 satellites, Mobile V2 is expected to feature
optimized and massive phased-array antennas to connect directly to unmodified LTE
smartphones. This will support seamless emergency texting, voice, standard data and
IoT transmissions outside of the coverage from traditional base transceiver stations. We
estimate the Mobile V2 satellite integrated approximately 3,000 – 4,000 independent
low- to mid-band cellular RF elements operating across the 1.6 to 2.7 GHz spectrum to
enable the D2C function.

Compound semi content growth is even more substantial
While the V3 platform expands overall RF content by roughly 4-5x versus V2, we believe
the increase in compound semiconductor content is even more pronounced. Based on
our analysis, Starlink’s V2 satellite relied heavily on Silicon-Germanium (SiGe BiCMOS)
and conventional Gallium Arsenide (GaAs) technologies for RF front-end modules,
particularly in Ku-band applications. As V3 pushes toward 1 Tbps throughput, we
believe the RF architecture is increasingly approaching the performance limits of SiGe-
based solutions, driving a meaningful migration toward higher performance compound
semiconductor technologies.

For V2, we estimate SiGe accounted for the vast majority of LNA content for Ku-band,
given its favourable integration with other components, lower cost, and low-noise
characteristics. GaAs was likely deployed in Ku-band PA, selective higher-frequency
backhaul applications (Ka, E- and V-band PAs), and certain LNAs. Among nearly ~7,500
PA and LNA devices for V2 satellite, we estimate ~45% were SiGe based with the
remaining ~55% utilizing GaAs technologies.

The material mix becomes substantially more favourable for compound semis in V3. As
operating frequencies extend further into Ka-, E-, V-, and newly introduced W-band
spectrum, the performance limitations of traditional SiGe architectures become
increasingly evident. Higher frequencies require improved power density, greater
efficiency, and superior thermal performance, particularly for high-capacity backhaul
links. We therefore expect most Ka-, E-, V-, and W-band power amplifiers within the V3
platform to migrate toward Gallium Nitride (GaN), given its superior electrical
characteristics, significantly higher power density, lower atmospheric loss, and stronger
thermal management capabilities. We estimate GaN can deliver roughly 4-8x higher
power density than conventional GaAs solutions, making it particularly attractive for
next-generation satellite payloads operating at extremely high frequencies. Within the
user-link payload, we believe Ku-band PAs will continue to adopt GaAs solutions.

For LNAs, we continue to believe SiGe will play an important role for backhaul receiver
applications given its superior noise performance, high integration capability, and cost
advantages. That said, we expect GaAs adoption to increase in performance-critical
applications for backhaul LNAs, where the demands of ultra-high-frequency operation
become increasingly challenging for silicon-based technologies.

Combining the higher RF channel count with the ongoing migration toward GaAs and
GaN, we estimate that V3 satellites will contain approximately 33,000 PA and LNA
devices in total. Of this, we estimate roughly 75% will be GaAs-based, ~13% SiGe-
based, and ~12% GaN-based. Under this framework, compound semiconductors (GaAs
+ GaN) would account for ~87% of total RF devices in V3, compared with only ~55% in
V2. As a result, we believe the compound semiconductor content opportunity could
expand by roughly 6-7x on a per-satellite basis, significantly outpacing the ~4-5x
increase in overall RF unit content and creating a disproportionately large growth
opportunity for suppliers like WIN Semi with exposure to advanced GaAs and GaN
technologies.

WIN Semi stands out as a key beneficiary of Starlink V3 upgrade cycle
We view WIN Semi as one of the primary beneficiaries of Starlink's migration from the
V2 to V3 satellite platform, given its established position in the compound semi supply
chain. Based on industry checks, discussion with management, and prior disclosures, we
believe WIN Semi has been a key foundry partner supporting Starlink's V2 RF front-end
devices, particularly for GaAs-based PAs and LNAs. As Starlink transitions toward V3
platform with higher throughput and wider adoption of D2C feature on Mobile V2, we
believe the substantial growth in RF content and higher adoption of GaAs/GaN
technologies meaningfully expand WIN Semi's growth opportunity.

According to press reports, US FCC has accepted SpaceX's filing of launching 100,000
Starlink V3 satellites, which is part of the larger scheme for up to 1 mn satellites. We
believe RF component production for V3 satellites has already begun in 2026, with
wafer demand poised to accelerate meaningfully in 2027-28E as deployment ramps.
Our base case assumes component builds for ~ 3,000 V3 satellites in 2027E, rising to
~4,500 satellites in 2028E, based on SpaceX's initial goal of launching up to 30,000 V3
satellites in the coming years. As the V3 satellite adopts substantially more GaAs and
GaN PAs/LNAs, we believe this will drive a strong revenue and earnings growth for WIN
Semi in 2027-30E.

The most attractive growth driver, in our view, is the emergence of GaN-based RF
content. As Starlink expands into E-, V-, and W-band applications, while simultaneously
increasing throughput and beamforming sophistication, we believe GaN adoption will
increase materially relative to the V2 generation. We estimate each V3 satellite could
initially consume the equivalent of roughly four 4” GaN wafers. There is additional
upside should future generations incorporate even higher-frequency D-band spectrum
(~110 – 170 GHz) , which would further strengthen the performance advantages of
GaN technologies.

Importantly, GaN offers substantially more attractive economics for WIN Semi than
conventional GaAs. We estimate GaN wafer ASPs of US$8,000-10,000 per wafer,
compared with ~US$2,000-3,000 for regular GaAs wafers. In addition, GaN also offers
10-20 ppt higher GM over matured GaAs-based process due to more sophisticated
manufacturing technology. As a result, even a modest increase in GaN wafer volume can
have a disproportionate impact on WIN Semi's earnings growth.

WIN Semi has already been investing to expand its GaN capacity in 2026 and we believe
the company is also evaluating additional capacity expansion initiatives, including
potential cleanroom and fab investments, as well as migrating from its current 4”
platform toward higher-productivity 6” production (2.25x area versus 4"). Given current
GaN capacity of less than 1,000 4” wafer/month, we believe its GaN capacity could
potentially double over the next 2 years, positioning WIN Semi to capture the
anticipated ramp in satellite-related demand at Starlink, as well as other potential
customers.

Earnings estimate revisions
We raise our 2027E and 2028E earnings forecasts for WIN Semi by 23% and 31%,
respectively, driven primarily by stronger growth in infrastructure and optical businesses.
Our revised estimates incorporate a more aggressive ramp in LEO satellite demand,
underpinned by Starlink's transition to the V3 and Mobile V2 platforms, along with the
associated increase in RF content per satellite. We estimate LEO satellite-related revenue
will account for ~10% of total sales in 2026E, representing ~30% of infrastructure
segment revenue. As Starlink V3 deployment accelerates, we expect this contribution to
expand to ~30% of total sales by 2028E. As a result, infrastructure revenue should
increase from ~35% of total sales in 2026E to ~50% by 2028E, becoming WIN Semi's
largest growth driver and reducing dependency on the more cyclical handset market.
Relative to VA consensus, our key point of differentiation is infrastructure sales outlook.
Following our deep-dive analysis of WIN Semi's LEO opportunity, we assume stronger
satellite deployments, higher RF content per satellite and faster migration from SiGe/
GaAs to higher-value GaAs/GaN solutions than currently reflected in consensus. While
our 2026E sales estimate is broadly in line, we forecast infrastructure revenue reaching
NT$13.3bn and NT$17.4bn in 2027E/2028E, versus consensus at NT$9.1bn and NT
$10.7bn, respectively. This implies infrastructure contributes 45.5% and 50.0% of total
sales in 2027E/2028E, compared with consensus expectations of 35.6% and 36.5%.

In addition to the volume opportunity, we expect a favourable product mix shift to
support profitability. The increasing adoption of higher-value GaN-based PAs for Starlink
V3, which we estimate carry gross margins 10-20 ppts above conventional GaAs
infrastructure products, should contribute to meaningful margin expansion. We
therefore forecast corporate gross margin to improve from 29.4% in 2026E to 37.1% by
2028E, driven by mix upgrade and operating leverage from higher infrastructure
utilization, with our gross margin estimates also above consensus (UBSe 34.9%/37.1%
vs consensus 32.6%/34.6%) in 2027/28E due to our higher infrastructure sales mix
assumptions.

Valuation: Raise price target to NT$725; reiterate Buy
WIN Semi stock has rebounded ~29% over the past three months versus ~3% for the
TAIEX, supported by a robust 2H26 outlook and improving sentiment toward its margin
and earnings profile. The stock has also re-rated and now trades at 39x/30x 2027/28E
UBS EPS, reflecting improving earnings visibility and a more diversified business mix with
less exposure to consumer end markets, including LEO satellite and optical
communications. While we believe the re-rating has been driven primarily by growing
confidence in the optical business ramp and better infrastructure outlook, we do not
believe the market has fully reflected WIN Semi's improving fundamentals and multi-
year earnings expansion cycle. Key earnings drivers are: 1) accelerating satellite-related
infrastructure demand; 2) rising optical and AI/datacom revenue contribution; and 3)
sustained margin recovery driven by a more favourable mix, improving loading, and
operating leverage. In particular, we believe the LEO satellite opportunity remains
underappreciated, and the successful Starship launch on 28 September should increase
investor's confidence in the pace of Starlink V3 deployment over the next several years,
supporting our above-consensus infrastructure growth and margin assumptions.

We raise our PT to NT$725 (from NT$500), as we roll over to 40x 2028E PE (from 40x
average 2027-28E), vs historical range of 10-57x, supported by a 2025-30E EPS CAGR
of 44%. We reiterate Buy, as WIN Semi is well positioned to capture the LEO satellite and
optical communication growth opportunities in 2026-28E, while its margins should
further advance on better product mix and operating leverage. Our 2027/28E EPS
estimates are 38%/45% above consensus, and we foresee potential upward revisions in
consensus earnings estimates being a catalyst.

Company Description
Established in 1999, WIN Semiconductors is a leading foundry for compound semiconductor
wafers globally, with 43k 6-inch wafer capacity per month as of end-2022. While it offers
different types of compound semiconductors (GaAs, GaN, InP, etc.), the GaAs compound
contributes the majority of its revenue. Its products are used to make signal power amplifiers
that customers use in networking equipment and communication devices, including base
stations and smartphones.


Valuation Method and Risk Statement
We value WIN Semi using PE relative to its historical trading range and peer average.
Investing in WIN Semi involves risks that include, but are not limited to, rapid technological
changes, increasing competition, exposure to macroeconomic cycles and uncertain
enddemand. Slower wireless technology migration and poor performances by customers
could also significantly affect WIN Semi’s fundamental performance. WIN Semi’s LEO satellite
customers may face execution challenges in launching satellites, which will impact WIN
Semi's infrastructure revenue growth outlook. On the other hand, its progress on developing
and qualifying the optical communication laser diodes will have a significant impact to its
earnings outlook and market sentiment. Moreover, it is extremely difficult to project the
financial results of tech companies, since their operating models are highly volatile and
unpredictable.

NYPCB (NANYF)
Our PO of NT$2,000 is based on 35x 2H27-1H28E P/E. We view this multiple as fair
given ROE and operating margin expansion to 39% and 41% in 2027-28E (vs 13% and
14% in 2025-26E).

Upside risks to our PO are (1) tighter ABF supply, (2) higher SiP/AiP adoption, and (3)
less intensified competition pressure in PCB business.

Downside risks are (1) greater ABF expansion from peers, (2) muted SiP/AiP adoption,
and (3) more severe competition in PCB business.
